# vivePDF · Documentation

> vivePDF documentation: installing, opening PDFs, organising pages, converting, OCR, signing, Studio, presenter view, shortcuts and troubleshooting.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/

---

# Installation

> How to install vivePDF on Windows 10/11 and macOS 14+, get past the SmartScreen and Gatekeeper warnings, receive updates and uninstall it.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

vivePDF is a free PDF editor for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and for Macs with Apple silicon on macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Download the installer from the releases page on GitHub and open it; you do not need an account, and the app does not need to stay online.

## Install on Windows

1. Download `vivePDF_<version>_x64-setup.exe` from the [latest release page](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases/latest).
2. Double-click the downloaded file and follow the installer.
3. When it finishes, open vivePDF from the Start menu. The first screen is Home, where you can open a PDF or go to the tools.

### The SmartScreen warning

The installer carries no code signature, so the first time you run it Windows may show **Windows protected your PC**. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. The warning is only about the installer; the app itself does not ask again.

> **Office conversions**
>
> Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversions use LibreOffice. It comes with the Windows installer and is set up without internet on the first start (about 900 MB on disk). You can remove or reinstall it in **Settings › Tools**.

## Updates

vivePDF checks for new versions itself. At start-up it only fetches version information; downloading and installing always ask you first. Updates are signed and arrive in small packages.

- To check by hand, open **Settings › Updates** and click **Check for updates**.
- When a new version is ready, choose **Download and install**; once the download finishes, **Restart** moves the app to the new version.
- If you do not want automatic checks, turn off **Check automatically at startup**. While [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) is on, no check is made at all.

What changed in each version is on the [Release notes](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/release-notes/) page.

## Install on macOS

1. Download `vivePDF_<version>_aarch64.dmg` from the [latest release page](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases/latest).
2. Open the DMG and drag vivePDF to **Applications**.
3. Open vivePDF from Applications or Launchpad.

### The Gatekeeper warning

The app is not notarised by Apple, so macOS may block the first start. Open **System Settings › Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway** next to the vivePDF message. If you prefer Terminal, `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/vivePDF.app` does the same. You only need this the first time.

Office conversions use the LibreOffice in Applications; if it is not installed, the app downloads it when you ask. Scanning needs SANE (`brew install sane-backends`).

## Linux

On Linux, vivePDF is [built from source](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/build-from-source/). The same steps work for development on Windows and macOS.

## Uninstall

On Windows, remove vivePDF from **Settings › Apps › Installed apps**; on a Mac, drag it from Applications to the Bin. If you also want to delete the settings and recent-file list the app keeps on this computer, use **Settings › Data** in vivePDF before uninstalling; **Help › Privacy** shows what is stored.

---

# Interface

> A tour of vivePDF's top bar, Tools menu, command palette, tabs, tab groups, windows and the side panels in the Viewer.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/interface/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

Everything in vivePDF starts from one bar along the top of the window. The **Home**, **Viewer**, **Pages** and **Studio** buttons on the left switch between workspaces, and the **Tools** and **Help** menus hold the rest. The documents you open sit in tabs, which you can group or move into separate windows.

## The top bar

The vivePDF logo and the four workspaces sit on the left of the bar:

- **Home**: recent documents, collections and quick tools. **Customize home** lets you rearrange its sections.
- **Viewer**: where you read, search and mark up documents. See [Open and read a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-and-read/).
- **Pages**: the page organizer, showing every page of the open document as a thumbnail. See [Organise pages](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/pages/).
- **Studio**: an editor for writing a document or making a design from a blank page.

On the right you will find the search box that opens the command palette, the theme button (it switches between light and dark), the **Language** menu, **Settings** (the gear icon) and the **Open PDF** button. When a new version is ready, a green update button appears to the left of the search box.

As the window gets narrower the bar compacts itself: labels go first, then the menus turn into icons, so search, settings and **Open PDF** stay visible at any width.

## The Tools menu

Click **Tools** and the menu opens in two parts. On the left are the thirteen categories, from **Page layout** and **Check** to **Security & signing** and **Automation**, each with the number of tools it holds. Point at a category, click it or move to it with the arrow keys, and its tools appear on the right with a short description of each. The menu opens on the category of the tool you are using.

**Show all** at the bottom of the menu opens the catalogue of every tool with a search box. **Search in folders** searches the text of every PDF in the folders you have indexed and jumps straight to the page. The full list is on the [Tools](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/tools/) page.

## The command palette

Press `Ctrl+K`, or click the **Search tools, pages or documents** box in the top bar, to open the command palette. Type the name of a tool, a settings section or an open document, pick it with the arrow keys and press `Enter`.

Start your search with a symbol to narrow the palette to one kind of result:

- `>` shows only actions, such as **New window**, **PDF from clipboard** or **Check for updates**.
- `/` searches pages and settings sections.
- `@` searches open documents and recent files.
- `#` followed by a number goes to that page of the open document.

## The Help menu

The **Help** menu holds **Help topics**, **Keyboard shortcuts (F1)**, **What's new** and **Privacy**. Below them come **Report a bug**, **Suggest a feature**, **Open log folder** and **Save support bundle…**, and at the bottom **Check for updates** and **About**.

> **Shortcuts for this screen**
>
> Wherever you are, `F1` or `Ctrl+/` shows the shortcuts for that screen, and `Shift+F1` opens its help topic. The full list is on the [Keyboard shortcuts](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/) page.

## Tabs and tab groups

Every document you open gets its own tab above the Viewer; the same tabs also appear in Pages. Drag a tab to change its place, or move it with `Ctrl+Shift+←`/`→`. `Ctrl+W` closes the active document.

Right-click a tab for options such as **Close others**, **Close all**, **Copy path**, **Copy file name**, **Show in folder** and **Open beside current document**. **Add to new group** in the same menu groups tabs the way a web browser does:

- Click the name chip in front of a group to collapse or expand it, double-click it to rename the group, and drag it to move the whole group.
- The group menu offers **Colour** (13 colours), **Ungroup**, **Close the group's documents**, **Open a document in this group** and **Save as collection**.
- A group saved as a collection appears under **Collections** on Home, where you can later reopen all its files as one tab group.

## Windows

`Ctrl+Shift+N` opens an empty new window. To give a document a window of its own, drag its tab out of the window and let go, or choose **Move to new window** from the tab menu; **Move group to new window** in the group menu moves all of the group's documents to a new window. A document with unsaved changes stays in its window until you save it. Settings, theme, language and recent files are shared by every window.

## Side panels in the Viewer

In the Viewer, a vertical strip of buttons runs down each side of the page.

The **Navigation** strip on the left opens the **Thumbnails**, **Outline** and **Attachments** panels. A **Signatures** button appears when the document is signed, and **Layers** when it has layers.

The **Tools** strip on the right starts with **Comments**, **Annotate / mark up**, **Edit** and **Presentation tools**. Then come **Reading mode**, **Read aloud**, **Page colours** and **Document info**. At the bottom of the strip are the page number box, **Rotate**, the **Page display** menu and the zoom buttons.

Each button opens and closes its own panel. You can choose which panels are ready when a document opens in **Settings › Viewer**; for the other settings see [Settings and privacy](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/settings-privacy/).

---

# First steps

> How to open a PDF the first time you start vivePDF, find the tool you need and see where the result is saved, with screenshots.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/first-steps/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

When you start vivePDF, the **Home** screen opens. To open a PDF, click **Open PDF** or drag the file onto the window; to reach a tool, use the **Tools** menu at the top or the command palette. Every tool writes its result to a new file, so your original stays as it was.

## 1. Open a document

1. On **Home**, click **Open PDF** or press `Ctrl+O` and choose your file.
2. Or drag the file from Finder or Explorer onto the window. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files and pictures open too.
3. The document opens in its own tab in the **Viewer**. Move between pages with the thumbnails on the left, and open the markup and editing tools from the strip on the right.

![The vivePDF Home screen: the Open PDF button, Quick access tools and Recent documents](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/start-1-1600.webp)

Documents you open stay in the **Recent documents** list, so next time they are one click away. The **Merge**, **Split**, **Compress** and other buttons in the **Quick access** row are shortcuts to the most used tools.

> **Shortcuts on a Mac**
>
> The `Ctrl` shortcuts in this guide use `⌘` on a Mac: `⌘+O` opens a document and `⌘+K` brings up the command palette. The full list is on the [Keyboard shortcuts](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/) page.

## 2. Find the tool you need

Every tool sits in the **Tools** menu at the top, sorted into thirteen categories by what it does, such as **Page layout**, **Check**, **From PDF**, **Create & design** and **Security & signing**. Point at a category on the left and its tools appear on the right.

![The Tools menu open: thirteen categories on the left, the Page layout tools with short descriptions on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/start-2-1600.webp)

If you don't know where a tool is, use the command palette: press `Ctrl+K` and type what you want to do. Typing "compress", for example, puts **Compress** at the top; `Enter` opens it.

![The command palette searching for 'compress' with the Compress tool as the first result](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/start-3-1600.webp)

## 3. Find the result

When you run a tool, the result appears in the panel on the right: the page count or the space saved, a preview and the name of the new file. By default the file is saved next to the original with a short addition to its name (for example `report-merged.pdf`). Change where it goes with **Browse** next to **Output file**.

The **Next step** buttons in the result panel carry on with the new file, for example to compress or password-protect the file you just merged. The book icon opens the result in the Viewer, and the folder icon shows the file in Finder or Explorer.

![A report open in the Viewer: page thumbnails on the left, the tool strip on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/start-4-1600.webp)

## What next?

Short guides for the most common jobs:

- [Merge PDFs](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/merge-pdfs/) and [split a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/split-a-pdf/)
- [Compress a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/compress-a-pdf/)
- [Convert a PDF to Word](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/pdf-to-word/), [convert Word to PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/office-to-pdf/) and [make a PDF from photos](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-to-pdf/)
- [Fill in a form](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/fill-a-form/), [sign a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign-a-pdf/) and [edit text in a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/edit-pdf-text/)
- [Highlight and annotate](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/highlight-and-annotate/) and [delete pages](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/delete-pages/)
- [Password-protect a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/password-protect-a-pdf/) and [redact a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/redact-a-pdf/)

The whole interface is described on the [Interface](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/interface/) page.

---

# Merge PDFs

> How to combine several PDFs into one file with vivePDF, put them in order, take only some pages and save the result, step by step.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/merge-pdfs/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To combine several PDFs into one file, open **Tools › Merge**, add the files, put them in order and click **Merge**. The original files are left untouched; the result is saved as a new PDF.

1. Open **Tools › Merge**, or click the **Merge** shortcut on Home.
2. Choose the PDFs with **Add files** or drag them onto the window. For every PDF in a folder, use **Add folder**.
3. Set the order: drag a row by its handle, or use the up and down arrows on the right.
4. To take only some pages of a file, type them in its **Page range** box, such as `1-3, 5`; leave it empty for every page.
5. Click **Merge**.

![The Merge tool: two PDFs in the list, page range boxes and the One after another option](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/merge-1-1600.webp)

The result appears in the panel on the right: the total page count, a preview of the first page and the name of the new file (for example `report-merged.pdf`). The book icon opens it, and the **Next step** buttons let you compress or protect it straight away.

![Merging finished: 8 pages, a preview and report-merged.pdf in the panel on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/merge-2-1600.webp)

## Useful options

- **Bookmarks**: adds a bookmark for each file and keeps the file's own bookmarks under it.
- **Add a contents page**: puts a list of the files with their page numbers on the first page.
- **Start every file on a front side**: keeps two files from sharing a sheet when you print double-sided.

> **Scanned the fronts and backs separately?**
>
> Under **How to combine**, choose **Alternate pages**. The fronts and backs are interleaved into one document, and if you scanned the backs starting from the last page, their order is reversed.

See the [Tools](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/tools/) page for more. To do the opposite and cut a PDF into parts, see [Split a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/split-a-pdf/).

---

# Compress a PDF

> How to make a PDF smaller with vivePDF, see what takes up the space, choose a compression profile and get a file small enough to e-mail.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/compress-a-pdf/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To make a PDF smaller, open **Tools › Compress**, choose your file, pick a profile and click **Compress**. Pictures are resampled and unused font parts and leftover structure are cleaned out; the original file stays as it was.

1. Open **Tools › Compress** and choose the PDF, or drag it onto the window.
2. Look at **What the file is made of**: pictures, fonts and page content are shown separately, with the largest pictures listed.
3. Pick a **Profile**. For e-mail, **Strong** is usually enough.
4. Click **Compress**.

![The Compress tool: a bar showing that pictures fill most of a 25 MB brochure, and a list of the largest pictures](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/compress-1-1600.webp)

The profiles differ like this:

- **Light**: leaves pictures alone and only cleans the structure and fonts.
- **Balanced**: 150 dpi and 75% JPEG; invisible on screen.
- **Strong**: 100 dpi and 60% JPEG; ideal for e-mail.
- **Extreme**: 72 dpi and 40% JPEG; the smallest file, at low quality.
- **Custom**: you set the resolution and quality yourself.

The result panel shows the percentage saved, the old and new size and a before-and-after preview. In the example below, a 25 MB brochure came down to 266 KB.

![Compression result: −99%, from 25.0 MB to 265.8 KB, with a before and after preview](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/compress-2-1600.webp)

> **Need to get under a set size?**
>
> Turn on **Compress to a target size** and enter the limit (for example 10 MB). vivePDF tries the profiles from light to strong and saves the first result that fits.

A text-heavy PDF that is already small gains little; the big savings come from large photos and scans. For scanned documents, also see [Make scanned pages searchable (OCR)](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/).

---

# Convert a PDF to Word

> How to turn a PDF into an editable Word (.docx) file with vivePDF, keeping tables, pictures, headers and footers, step by step.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/pdf-to-word/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To convert a PDF to Word, open **Tools › Convert**, choose **PDF → Word** on the left, add your file and click **Convert**. The result is a .docx file you can edit in Word or LibreOffice, with its tables and pictures carried over.

1. Open **Tools › Convert** and choose **PDF → Word** in the list on the left.
2. Choose the PDF, or drag it onto the window.
3. If you only need some pages, type them in the **Pages** box, such as `1-3, 5`; leave it empty to convert every page.
4. Click **Convert**.

![PDF → Word selected in the Convert tool: agreement.pdf, the Pages box and the output file](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/word-1-1600.webp)

The new .docx file appears in the result panel. The button next to it opens the file in its default app, and the folder icon shows it in Finder or Explorer.

![Conversion finished: 1 file and agreement.docx in the panel on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/word-2-1600.webp)

With **Move repeated headers and footers into Word** on, text repeated at the top or bottom of most pages becomes Word's own header and footer instead of body text, and page numbers turn into Word's page number field.

> **Scanned PDFs**
>
> The pages of a scanned document are pictures; with no selectable text in them, Word gets only pictures too. Recognise the text with [OCR](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/) first, then convert to Word.

The same tool converts PDFs to Excel, PowerPoint, pictures, text and HTML. Every format is listed on the [Convert files](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/convert/) page.

---

# Convert Word, Excel and PowerPoint to PDF

> How to turn Word, Excel, PowerPoint and other Office files into PDFs with vivePDF, convert several files at once and set up LibreOffice.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/office-to-pdf/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To turn a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file into a PDF, open **Tools › Convert**, choose **Office → PDF** on the left, add the file and click **Convert**. LibreOffice does the Office conversion; if it is not on your computer, vivePDF offers to set it up.

1. Open **Tools › Convert** and choose **Office → PDF** in the list on the left.
2. Choose .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .odt and similar files with **Add files**, or drag them onto the window. You can add more than one.
3. Rename the **Output file** if you like; **Browse** picks another folder.
4. Click **Convert**.

![Office → PDF selected in the Convert tool: agreement.docx in the list, Paper size and the output file](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/office-1-1600.webp)

The result panel shows the page count and a preview of the first page. Under **Next step** you can compress the PDF or run OCR on it straight away.

![Conversion finished: a preview of the 2-page PDF and agreement-word.pdf](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/office-2-1600.webp)

> **LibreOffice is set up once**
>
> LibreOffice is free. If it is missing, vivePDF opens its download page from the **LibreOffice is needed** window, and the conversion carries on once it is installed. TXT, Markdown, HTML, EPUB, XPS and pictures convert without LibreOffice; **Paper size** applies to those files.

A quicker way: right-click the Office file in Finder or Explorer and choose **Open With › vivePDF**. It opens as a PDF copy, which you keep with **Save as PDF…**. More on the [Convert files](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/convert/) page.

---

# Make a PDF from photos

> How to combine photos, scans or a whole folder of pictures into one PDF with vivePDF, and choose the paper size, orientation and margin.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-to-pdf/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To make a PDF from photos, open **Tools › Convert**, choose **Images → PDF** on the left, add the pictures and click **Convert**. Each picture becomes a page; JPG, PNG, HEIC, WebP, TIFF and many other picture types are supported.

1. Open **Tools › Convert** and choose **Images → PDF** in the list on the left.
2. Choose the pictures with **Add images**, or drag them onto the window. For a whole folder, use **Add folder**.
3. Set the order with the up and down arrows.
4. Choose the **Paper size**, the **Orientation** and how each picture is placed: **Fit whole image** never crops, **Fill the page** covers the page edge to edge.
5. Click **Convert**.

![Images → PDF: three photos in the list, A4 paper, automatic orientation and Fit whole image selected](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/images-1-1600.webp)

With the orientation on automatic, landscape photos go on landscape pages and portrait photos on portrait pages. **Margin** leaves a white border around each picture.

![Conversion finished: a preview of the 3-page PDF and photos.pdf](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/images-2-1600.webp)

> **Photos of paper documents**
>
> If you photographed a paper document with your phone, **From photo** in **Tools › Scans** gives a better result: it finds the corners of the sheet, straightens the perspective and whitens the background.

Every conversion option is on the [Convert files](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/convert/) page.

---

# Fill in a PDF form

> How to open a fillable PDF form in vivePDF, type into its fields, tick its boxes and save the filled-in form, step by step.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/fill-a-form/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To fill in a PDF form, open it in vivePDF, click a field, type and press **Save**. When a form has fillable fields, vivePDF tells you in a bar above the document; there is no separate tool to open.

1. Open the form with **Open PDF** or by dragging it onto the window. The bar **This document has fillable form fields.** appears at the top.
2. If the fields are hard to see, click **Highlight fields**.
3. Click a field and type. Press `Tab` for the next field and `Shift+Tab` for the previous one. Click check boxes and options to tick them.
4. When you are done, click **Save** next to **Unsaved changes** in the toolbar.

![A filled-in course application form in the Viewer: name, e-mail, phone and course fields filled](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/form-1-1600.webp)

**Save** writes the changes into the form itself; to keep an empty copy too, make a copy of the file before you start. If you change your mind, the cross next to **Save** discards the changes.

## Forms without fields

Some forms are only lines with nothing to click. To fill those in, open **Edit** from the strip on the right and click the empty space where you want to write; a new text box opens there. See [Edit text in a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/edit-pdf-text/).

> **Signing the form**
>
> If the form needs your signature, see [Sign a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign-a-pdf/). To build a form of your own, use **Tools › Forms**.

---

# Sign a PDF

> How to sign a PDF by hand in vivePDF: draw your signature or take it from a photo, save it, place it on the page and set its size.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign-a-pdf/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To sign a PDF, open it, click **Edit** in the strip on the right, choose **Page tools › Place signature**, draw your signature and place it on the page. The signed document is saved as a new file; your original stays as it was.

1. Open the document in the Viewer and click **Edit** in the strip on the right.
2. In the bar at the top, choose **Place signature** from the **Page tools** menu.
3. Click **New** and draw your signature with a mouse, pen or finger. To use a photo of your signature on paper, choose **From photo**. Click **Save signature**.
4. Click where the signature goes, drag it into place and change its size with the **Width** slider.
5. Click **Apply signature**.

![The Signatures window: a signature drawn in the Draw a signature area, with Clear, From photo and Save signature](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/sign-1-1600.webp)

A saved signature is ready next time, so you don't have to draw it again. It is kept on this computer and never sent anywhere.

![The signature placed on the Client line of the agreement; the Width slider and Apply signature in the bar at the top](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/sign-3-1600.webp)

After **Apply signature**, the signed copy (for example `agreement-signed.pdf`) opens in a new tab.

![The signed agreement open in a new tab, with a Signed: agreement-signed.pdf message in the corner](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/sign-4-1600.webp)

> **A drawn signature is not a digital signature**
>
> A drawn signature is a picture on the page; it does not prove the document was not changed afterwards. For formal documents you can sign with a .p12 or .pfx certificate; see [Sign and verify](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign/).

---

# Edit text in a PDF

> How to correct the text in a PDF with vivePDF: click a paragraph and change it, add a new text box and save the change, step by step.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/edit-pdf-text/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To change the text in a PDF, open it, click **Edit** in the strip on the right, click the paragraph you want to change and type. The font, size and colour are in the panel on the right; when you are done, press **Save** or **Save as…**.

1. Open the document in the Viewer and click **Edit** in the strip on the right. **Edit text** is selected in the bar at the top.
2. Click the paragraph you want to change; a frame appears around it. Correct the text as in any text box.
3. To add new text, click an empty spot on the page; a new text box opens there.
4. Change the font, size and colour in the **Edit** panel on the right. Press `Ctrl+Z` to undo a step.
5. **Save** (`Ctrl+S`) writes the change into the file itself; to keep the original, choose **Save as…** (`Ctrl+Shift+S`) and give the new file a name.

![Editing text: the delivery time in Clause 2 changed from 45 to 60 days, with the Layers panel on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/edit-1-1600.webp)

The **Layers** list on the right shows every text and picture on the page. The eye icon hides an item, and the lock icon keeps it from being changed by accident.

## Pictures and other items

Switch to **Edit pictures** in the bar at the top to move, resize, replace or delete the pictures on the page. The **Add** menu puts new items on the page, such as a text box, picture, shape, table, chart or formula.

> **Scanned pages have no text to edit**
>
> A scanned page is one big picture. To edit its words, recognise the text with [OCR](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/) first.

If you only want to remove some words and cover them with a box nobody can read, use [redaction](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/redact-a-pdf/) instead of editing; edited text can survive elsewhere in the file.

---

# Highlight and annotate a PDF

> How to highlight, underline or strike out text in a PDF with vivePDF, draw with a pen, add shapes and text boxes, write notes on marks and save.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/highlight-and-annotate/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To highlight text in a PDF, open **Annotate / mark up** from the strip on the right, choose **Highlight** and drag over the text. Change the colour and opacity of your marks in the bar at the top, and press **Save** or **Save as** when you are done.

1. Open the document in the Viewer and click **Annotate / mark up** in the strip on the right. The markup bar opens at the top.
2. Choose **Highlight** and drag over the text you want to highlight.
3. Change the colour and opacity with **Colour** and **Opacity** on the second row of the bar.
4. To add a note to a mark, click it and choose **Note** in the small menu that appears.
5. **Save** writes the marks into the original file (it asks first); for a separate copy, choose **Save as**.

![The markup bar open; part of the agreement's first sentence highlighted in yellow, with note and delete buttons under it](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/annot-1-1600.webp)

The other tools in the bar:

- **Underline**, **Strikeout** and **Squiggly**: mark the text with a line instead of a highlight.
- **Pen**: free drawing; the **Eraser** rubs out part of a drawing.
- **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** and **Arrow**: put shapes on the page.
- **Text box**: adds writing anywhere on the page.

When you select text, the small menu that appears also has a **Highlight** button, for a quick highlight without opening the bar.

> **All your notes in one place**
>
> After saving, the **Comments** panel in the strip on the right lists every mark and note by page. From there you can reply, mark a note resolved, or export the notes as Markdown, XFDF or FDF.

Other features that help while reading are on the [Open and read a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-and-read/) page.

---

# Delete pages from a PDF

> How to select the pages you don't want in a PDF and delete them with the vivePDF page organizer, then save the result to a new file.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/delete-pages/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To delete pages from a PDF, open it, switch to **Pages** in the top bar, select the pages, press `Delete` and click **Apply and save**. The result is written to a new file; your original stays as it was.

1. Open the document and click **Pages** in the top bar. Every page is laid out as a thumbnail.
2. Click the page you want to delete. For several pages, `Ctrl`-click them one by one, `Shift`-click a range, or tick the boxes in the corners of the cards.
3. Press `Delete` or click the bin icon in the bar at the bottom. The selected pages leave the list at once.
4. Check the **Output file** name on the right and click **Apply and save**.

![The page organizer with a 6-page report; the last page selected and the 1 page selected bar at the bottom](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/pages-2-1600.webp)

Deleted the wrong page? Press `Ctrl+Z`; nothing is written to the file until you press **Apply and save**.

![The page deleted and saved: 5 pages left, report-edited.pdf and a preview in the panel on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/pages-4-1600.webp)

> **Changing the original file instead**
>
> Turn on **Overwrite the original file** to apply the change to the original instead of a new file. This cannot be undone, so leave it off if you are unsure.

The same screen lets you reorder pages by dragging, rotate them, add pages from another PDF and extract the selected pages to a separate file. All of it is on the [Organise pages](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/pages/) page.

---

# Split a PDF

> How to split a PDF into separate files with vivePDF by page ranges, a fixed number of pages, file size or bookmarks, step by step.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/split-a-pdf/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To cut a PDF into parts, open **Tools › Split**, choose your file, pick a split method and click **Split**. Each part is saved as its own PDF in a new folder next to the original.

1. Open **Tools › Split**, or click the **Split** shortcut on Home, and choose the PDF.
2. Pick a **Split method**. To pull out particular groups of pages, **By ranges** is the most flexible.
3. Type the ranges in the **Parts** box, separated by semicolons: `1-2; 3-4; 5-6` makes three files. To pick the pages by looking at them, click **Choose on pages**.
4. Click **Split**.

![The Split tool: By ranges selected, 1-2; 3-4; 5-6 in the Parts box and 3 parts in the panel on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/split-2-1600.webp)

The other methods:

- **Every N pages**: cuts the document into parts with the same number of pages.
- **Into N files**: splits the document into as many equal files as you ask for.
- **Single pages**: makes every page a file of its own.
- **By size**: no part goes over the MB limit you set; handy for e-mail attachments.
- **Odd / even**: puts the odd and even pages into separate files.
- **By bookmarks**: every bookmark at the chosen level starts a new part; ideal for chapters.
- **By text**: a new part starts on every page where the text you search for appears.

> **Only need a few pages?**
>
> To take a few pages out into one file, select them in the [page organizer](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/pages/) and use **Extract selected** instead of splitting.

To put the parts back together, see [Merge PDFs](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/merge-pdfs/).

---

# Password-protect a PDF

> How to protect a PDF with a password and AES-256 encryption in vivePDF, limit printing and copying, and keep the owner password safe.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/password-protect-a-pdf/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To put a password on a PDF, open **Tools › Security**, choose your file, type the **Open password** twice and click **Add password**. The protected copy is saved as a new file; your original stays as it was.

1. Open **Tools › Security**; the page opens on **Add password**. Choose the PDF, or drag it onto the window.
2. Type the **Open password** and type it again in **Confirm password**. The bar below shows how strong the password is.
3. Leave **Encryption** on **AES-256 (recommended)**.
4. To limit printing or copying, pick **Read only**, **No copying** or **Most restricted** under **Quick set** in the **Permissions** section.
5. Click **Add password**.

![Add password: Open password and Confirm password filled in, the strength bar at Strong and AES-256 selected](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/password-1-1600.webp)

If you left the **Owner password** empty, vivePDF makes up a random owner password and shows it once in the result panel. It is the only way to change the permissions later, so copy it with the button next to it and keep it somewhere safe.

![Password added: 2 pages, a preview and the Owner password created box in the panel on the right](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/password-2-1600.webp)

> **Don't forget the password**
>
> If you forget the open password, nobody can open the file, vivePDF included. Keep it in a password manager.

Removing a password, sealing with a certificate, watermarks and the other security tools are on the [Security](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/security/) page.

---

# Redact a PDF

> How to permanently remove names, amounts, ID numbers and other sensitive details from a PDF with vivePDF and cover them with a black box.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/redact-a-pdf/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To remove sensitive information from a PDF for good, open **Redaction** under **Tools › Security**, choose your file, type the text to hide and click **Redact**. Matching text is deleted from the file and covered with a box; the redacted copy is saved as a new file.

1. Open **Tools › Security**, click **Security** above the page title and choose **Redaction** from the list. Choose the PDF.
2. Type a word you want to hide in **Text to find** and press `Enter`. Each one is added as a separate tag.
3. Check the **Sensitive data found** list: if vivePDF finds ID numbers, IBANs or e-mail addresses in the document, it lists them here so you can add them with one click.
4. If you like, type a note such as `GDPR` in **Text on the box** and pick a **Box colour**.
5. Click **Redact**.

![Redaction: a name and an amount in Text to find; black boxes in the before and after preview on the right, 3 redactions](https://vivepdf.com/shots/en/redact-2-1600.webp)

The result panel shows how many places were redacted and a before-and-after preview. With **Also remove matches outside the page** on, the same text is also removed from comments, form fields, bookmarks and document properties, and vivePDF tells you how many places that was.

> **Drawing a black box is not enough**
>
> A black rectangle drawn over text does not hide it; the text stays underneath and can be copied. Redaction really deletes it from the file. This cannot be undone, so keep your original.

## Redacting an area by hand

To black out a signature, a photo or any other area, open the document in the Viewer, click **Edit** in the strip on the right, choose **Page tools › Black out area**, drag over the area and click **Black out**.

Regular expressions and the other options are on the [Security](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/security/) page.

---

# Open and read a PDF

> How to open documents in vivePDF, move between pages, search the text, zoom, change the page display, split the window and read comfortably.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-and-read/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

To open a PDF in vivePDF, click **Open PDF** on Home or in the top bar, or press `Ctrl+O`. The document opens in its own tab in the Viewer, where you can move between pages, search the text and zoom.

## Open a document

1. On Home, click **Open PDF** or press `Ctrl+O`, then choose your file.
2. Or drag files straight onto the window. If you drop several, each one opens in its own tab.
3. If the document is encrypted, **Password required** appears; type the password and the document opens.

You are not limited to PDFs: Office documents, e-books, e-mails and pictures dropped on the window open as a PDF copy. Changes to that copy stay temporary until you keep them with **Save as PDF…**. If you have copied a picture or some text, `Ctrl+Shift+V` turns it into a PDF.

You can also send a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file to vivePDF by right-clicking it in Explorer or Finder and choosing **Open With › vivePDF**. LibreOffice turns Office files into PDFs; when it is not on your computer, vivePDF offers to set it up in the **LibreOffice is needed** window and opens the file once it is ready. LibreOffice is free and only needs setting up once.

Very large files open too: vivePDF reads the document in pieces instead of loading it into memory all at once.

### Recent documents and sessions

Documents you open stay in the **Recent documents** list on Home. Pin the ones you use often and they are kept in a group of their own at the top. The **Restore last session** action in the command palette brings back the tabs that were open when you last closed the app. When you reopen a document, vivePDF continues where you left off; to read from the start, click **Go to page 1** in the notice.

## Move between pages

- Type a page number in the box at the bottom of the right-hand strip, or use its arrows to go to the previous or next page. If the document has page labels such as iii or A-1, you can type those as well.
- `Page Up`/`Page Down` and the left and right arrow keys change page, and `Home`/`End` go to the first and last page.
- After jumping to another page through a link or the outline, `Alt+←` takes you back and `Alt+→` forward again.
- The **Thumbnails** panel on the left shows every page, and the **Outline** panel lists the document's bookmarks.

## Search the document

`Ctrl+F` opens the search bar. Type the word you are looking for; the results are listed grouped by page. **Match case** and **Whole word** narrow them down. `F3` moves to the next result and `Shift+F3` to the previous one.

> **Searching scanned pages**
>
> Search only works on pages that have a text layer. If a scanned document returns no results, make its pages searchable with [OCR](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/) first.

## Zoom and page display

`Ctrl++` and `Ctrl+-`, or the mouse wheel with `Ctrl` held down, zoom in and out. `Ctrl+0` picks **Actual size**, `Ctrl+1` **Fit width** and `Ctrl+2` **Fit page**. To move the page around, hold `Space` and drag.

The **Page display** menu in the right-hand strip offers:

- **Single page**, **Two pages side by side** or **Two pages, cover page alone**
- **Vertical scrolling** or **Horizontal scrolling**
- **Automatic scrolling** (`Ctrl+Shift+H`); while it runs, the up and down arrows change the speed and `Esc` stops it
- **Page colours**: **Sepia**, **Dark (inverted)** or easy-on-the-eyes options such as white, yellow or green text on black

### Split window

`Ctrl+Shift+E` splits the window in two. From **Page display › Split window** you can place the panes **Side by side** or **Stacked**, and **Compare with another document…** opens a different file in the second pane. **Sync scrolling** keeps both panes moving together.

## Comfortable reading

- **Reading mode** shows the text of the page in a single column. You can make the text larger or smaller and choose the column width and the **Paper**, **Sepia** or **Dark** theme.
- **Read aloud** reads the document in the voice and at the speed you choose.
- `F11` switches to immersive mode and shows the document full screen. If you want to present it, see [Present a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/present/).
- `Ctrl+P` opens the print dialog.

Every Viewer shortcut is listed on the [Keyboard shortcuts](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/) page, and the overall layout of the screen is described under [Interface](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/interface/).

---

# Organise pages

> How to reorder, rotate, delete, insert, extract and split PDF pages with the vivePDF page organizer, and what happens to the original file.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/pages/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

The page organizer is where you reorder, rotate, delete, insert and split pages in vivePDF. Open a document, then click **Pages** in the top bar to see every page as a thumbnail. Nothing touches the file until you press **Apply and save**, and by default the result is written to a new file.

## The basic flow

1. Open the document in the Viewer, then choose **Pages** in the top bar. The organizer always works on the document open in the Viewer.
2. Select pages and drag them to their new place.
3. Rotate, delete, insert or mark where to split. Every step can be undone with `Ctrl+Z` and redone with `Ctrl+Y`.
4. Click **Apply and save** or press `Ctrl+Enter`. The new file goes where the save field at the bottom shows.

## Select pages

Click a page to select it and double-click to preview it. For several pages, `Shift`- or `Ctrl`-click, tick the box in a card's corner, or drag across an empty area. `Ctrl+A` selects them all and `Esc` clears the selection.

The **Select** menu in the toolbar goes further:

- **Select by page numbers** (`Ctrl+G`): type ranges such as `1-5, 9, 12-`.
- **Select odd pages**, **Select even pages**, **Invert selection**
- **Select blank pages**, **Select scanned pages**, **Find duplicate pages**
- **Select by text…**: selects the pages that contain a given piece of text.
- Selection **By page size**, or portrait and landscape pages

## Reorder, rotate and delete

Drag pages to reorder them. To move the selected pages to a particular position, press `M` and type the page number.

The **Edit pages** menu holds:

- **Rotate left** and **Rotate right** (`Shift+R` / `R`)
- **Duplicate** (`Ctrl+D`) and **Make copies…**
- **Delete selected** (`Delete`), plus deleting every page before or after one
- **Reverse order** and **Reverse selected pages**
- **Fix page orientation**: finds pages lying sideways or upside down and turns them.
- **Prepare for two-sided printing**: arranges fronts and backs for printers without automatic duplex.
- **Page labels**: gives pages a cover label or numbers such as i, ii, iii.

When you point at a card, buttons to rotate or delete that page alone appear on it too.

## Insert pages

From the **Insert** menu choose **Insert blank page** (`B`), **Insert pages from PDF** or **Insert pages from images**. For blank pages you can pick the paper size, the orientation and a paper pattern such as lined, graph or dot grid. You also decide whether new pages go before the selection, after it or at the end. **Replace selected pages with pages from a PDF** swaps the selection for pages from another file.

> **Moving pages between documents**
>
> Copy the selected pages with `Ctrl+C`, switch to another document's tab and paste them with `Ctrl+V`. Dragging pages onto another document's tab copies them to the end of that document.

## Split and extract

- To split, select pages and press `S`, or use **Split › Split after selected pages**. **Split at chapters (bookmarks)** cuts the document at every chapter start, and **Remove split marks** (`Shift+S`) clears them all. When the marks are in place, click **Save as separate files**.
- To make a new PDF from the selected pages only, choose **Extract selected** or press `Ctrl+E`.
- In the **Export** menu, **Save as pictures…** saves pages as image files and **Print…** prints the selected pages, or all of them.

## What happens to the original?

By default **Apply and save** writes the result to a new file and the original stays as it was. To write the change straight into the original, turn on **Overwrite the original file**; the button then reads **Apply to original**. If the document has unsaved changes in the Viewer, vivePDF asks you to save or discard them first. You can choose where new files are saved by default in **Settings › Files**.

## Separate page tools

Use **Tools › Merge** to combine several PDFs into one file, and **Tools › Split** to break a PDF up by page ranges, a fixed page count, file size or bookmarks. There are also separate tools for rotating, deleting and extracting pages; they are all listed on the [Tools](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/tools/) page.

In the organizer, the `?` key shows every shortcut; for the full list see [Keyboard shortcuts](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/). If you want scanned pages to be searchable once they are in order, the [OCR](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/) page explains how.

---

# Convert files

> How vivePDF turns PDFs into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, pictures, text, Markdown, HTML and EPUB, and makes PDFs from pictures, Office files, SVG and web pages.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/convert/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

vivePDF converts PDFs into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, pictures, text, Markdown, HTML and EPUB, and makes PDFs from pictures, Office documents, SVG drawings and web pages. Everything lives in one tool, **Tools › Convert**, and your files are converted on your own computer.

## How to convert

1. Open **Tools › Convert**. In the Tools menu it sits in the **From PDF** group.
2. Pick a conversion from the list on the left: the options under **From PDF** turn a PDF into another format, and those under **To PDF** create a PDF.
3. Choose your file and check the options. When converting from a PDF, type a page range if you only want some of the pages.
4. Click **Convert**. When it finishes, **Open output folder** in the result panel on the right takes you to the new file.

## From PDF to other formats

- **PDF → Word**: makes a layout-preserving .docx with its tables and images. With **Move repeated headers and footers into Word** on, text repeated on most pages becomes the Word header and footer, and page numbers become a Word page number field.
- **PDF → Excel**: tables on the pages go to separate worksheets; the text of pages without a table goes line by line to a sheet of its own. You can choose .xlsx or .csv as the file type, and lay out the tables **One per table**, **One per page** or **All tables on one sheet**. **Also find tables without lines** reads columns lined up by spacing alone as well.
- **PDF → PowerPoint**: each page becomes a slide. With **Editable text**, the text goes into editable boxes over a picture of the rest of the page; **Picture only** places an exact picture of each page and puts the page text into the speaker notes.
- **PDF → JPG / PNG**: each page becomes a picture. Choose PNG, JPG, WebP or TIFF and a resolution (DPI) from 72 to 600. There are also options to join the pages into one tall picture, make a single multi-page TIFF, pack the pictures into one ZIP file, save in greyscale or keep a transparent background.
- **Extract images**: saves every picture embedded in the pages at its original resolution.
- **PDF → Text**, **PDF → Markdown**, **PDF → HTML**: give you plain text, Markdown that keeps headings and tables, or a single HTML file with one section per page. For Markdown you can leave pictures out, save them in a folder next to the file or put them inside the file.
- **PDF → EPUB**: makes a reflowable e-book for phones and e-readers. You can choose how chapters are divided, the book title, the author and whether the first page is the cover.

> **Scanned PDFs**
>
> A scanned page holds a picture rather than text. For Text, Markdown, HTML and EPUB, turn on **Read pages without text with OCR**; the PDF itself is not changed. For Word, Excel and PowerPoint, run [OCR](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/) on the document first, then convert it.

## From other files to PDF

- **Images → PDF**: combines pictures, or a whole folder of them, into one PDF. You can **Include subfolders**, sort by name or date, set a margin, and choose whether each picture fits on the page or fills it.
- **Office → PDF**: Word, Excel and PowerPoint documents are converted with LibreOffice. TXT, Markdown, HTML, EPUB, XPS, CBZ and picture files convert directly.
- **SVG → PDF**: turns drawings from Inkscape, Illustrator or Figma into vector PDF pages at their own size. With **Put every drawing in one PDF** on, each drawing becomes a page of the same file.
- **Web page → PDF**: downloads a web address and saves it as a PDF. **Reader mode** keeps only the main article and leaves menus and sidebars out; **Include pictures** adds or drops the pictures.

> **The one conversion that needs internet**
>
> **Web page → PDF** goes online to download the page, so it is not available while [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) is on. Every other conversion runs on your computer without internet.

### LibreOffice

Office conversions use LibreOffice. It comes with the Windows installer, and you can remove or reinstall it in **Settings › Tools**. Without LibreOffice, Office files you add to the list show a **needs LibreOffice** warning. Setup details are on the [Installation](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/) page.

## Where the result is saved

By default the new file is written next to the source, with a suffix that names the tool. In **Settings › Files** you can switch **Where to save** to **Fixed folder** and pick an output folder, and use the name pattern to decide how files are named. Converting never changes your original file.

> **Just reading?**
>
> If you only want to read a Word document, an e-book or a picture, you do not need to convert it: drop it on the window and it opens as a PDF copy. See [Open and read a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-and-read/).

---

# Make scanned pages searchable (OCR)

> How to add a searchable text layer to scanned PDFs with OCR in vivePDF, manage OCR languages, scan from a scanner and clean up scans.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

The pages of a scanned PDF are really pictures: you cannot search them or select and copy their text. vivePDF's OCR tool reads the pages and adds an invisible text layer on top of them. The pages look the same, but their text can now be searched, selected and copied. OCR runs on your computer with the built-in Tesseract, and your document is not sent anywhere.

## Run OCR

1. Open **Tools › OCR** and pick the scanned PDF. vivePDF shows how many pages are scanned and how many already have a text layer.
2. Under **Languages**, tick the languages that appear in the document.
3. Choose the **Scope**, and turn on **Auto-rotate** and **Clean up before reading** if you need them.
4. Click **Run OCR**. The result is written to a new file; your original stays as it was.

When it finishes, the result panel shows how many pages were recognised, how many were skipped and how many were turned upright.

## Languages

The language list only shows installed languages, and at first the app language and English are ticked. Turkish and English come with vivePDF. Pick only the languages that really appear in the document: each extra language slows reading down and can add mistakes.

If you need another language, open **Download more languages** on the OCR page, or use the **OCR language packs** list in **Settings › Tools**. Each language is downloaded once and then works without internet. The **Default OCR language** setting decides which language is ticked when the OCR page opens.

> **Downloading a language needs internet**
>
> Language packs are downloaded from the tessdata repository. While [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) is on, no new language can be downloaded; OCR with the languages you already have always works.

## Options

The **Scope** decides which pages are read:

- **Scanned pages only**: pages that already contain text stay untouched. This is the right choice for most documents.
- **All pages**: every page is read again and any existing text layer is replaced.
- **Redo old OCR**: the hidden text from an earlier OCR is removed and the page is read again; pages with visible text stay as they are.

The other options:

- **Auto-rotate**: finds the reading direction of pages scanned sideways or upside down and puts them right; it makes the run a little slower.
- **Clean up before reading**: fixes contrast and reduces specks. It is used only for reading, so the page looks the same.
- **Recognition resolution**: 150, 200 or 300. 200 is enough for most documents; 300 is more accurate but slower.
- **Pages**: type a range to read only some pages. If the document mixes scanned pages and pages with text, the **Process scanned pages only** button fills in the range for you.
- **Also save the text**: also writes the recognised text next to the PDF as plain text (.txt) or a Word document (.docx).

## Quick OCR from the Viewer

You can also recognise text without opening the tool. In the Viewer, right-click an empty part of the page and choose **Make selectable › Make this page selectable** or **Make the whole document selectable**.

> **This changes the file itself**
>
> Unlike the OCR tool, **Make selectable** does not create a new file: it writes the text layer into the open document and the file is rewritten on disk. The page looks exactly the same and pages that already have text are left alone, but the change cannot be undone.

If you only need the text of a small part, use the Viewer's **Text from an area** tool and drag over that area; vivePDF reads the text there and shows it so you can copy it.

## The Scans tool

Jobs that take you from paper to PDF are gathered in **Tools › Scans**:

- **From scanner**: scans straight from your scanner. On Windows your scanner is listed directly; on macOS and Linux SANE must be installed. It offers **Scan both sides** and **Skip blank sheets**, and with **Make the text searchable (OCR)** on, the scanned pages are read as they are saved.
- **Enhance**: cleans up existing scans with **Straighten** (for tilted pages), **Remove speckles**, **Whiten background**, **Remove edge shadows** and **Remove blank pages**. **Show preview** shows the page before and after.
- **Split batch**: splits a stack scanned in one go into separate files at blank pages, at QR or barcode separator sheets, or wherever a text pattern is found.
- **From photo**: finds the corners of paper in phone photos, straightens the perspective, whitens the background and turns each photo into a page.

## After OCR

Once a document has been through OCR, [search in the Viewer](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-and-read/) works on it. To turn a scanned document into Word or Excel, run OCR first, then follow the steps on the [Convert files](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/convert/) page.

---

# Sign and verify

> How to add a hand-drawn signature, sign a PDF digitally with a .p12 or .pfx certificate, verify signatures and create a certificate in vivePDF.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

vivePDF offers two kinds of signature: a hand-drawn signature that you place on the page as a picture in the Viewer, and a digital signature made with a .p12 or .pfx certificate in **Tools › Sign**. From the same place you can verify a signed file, create your own certificate and export its public part. Everything runs on this computer; neither the document nor the certificate is sent anywhere.

## Hand-drawn signature

A hand-drawn signature goes onto the page as a picture. It is quick for signing a form or a letter, but it does not prove whether the document changed afterwards.

1. Open the document in the Viewer and click **Edit** in the toolbar.
2. From the **Page tools** menu, choose **Place signature**.
3. Draw a signature with **New** using a mouse, pen or your finger, or take one **From photo**. If you will use it again, click **Save signature**; next time you can pick it from **Saved signatures**.
4. Click where the signature goes, drag it into place and choose **Apply signature**.

The result is written to a new file and opened straight away; your original stays as it was. Saved signatures can be removed in **Settings › Data**.

## Digital signature with a certificate

A digital signature shows who signed the document and that it has not changed since. vivePDF applies a PAdES signature.

1. Open **Tools › Sign** and choose the PDF to sign.
2. Under **Certificate file (.p12 / .pfx)**, pick the file from your e-signature provider or one created in vivePDF, and enter the **Certificate password**.
3. If the signature should be visible, turn on **Visible signature box on the page**, then choose the page, the **Box text** and, if you like, a saved handwritten signature or a logo as the **Picture in the signature box**.
4. Fill in **Reason**, **Location** and **Contact** if needed, then click **Sign**.

If the document already has empty signature fields, choose one under **Signature field**; the signature then uses that field's place and size.

### Extra options

- **Timestamp server (optional)**: enter an RFC 3161 server address to add a trusted time to the signature. It needs the internet, and only a digest of the signature is sent to that server.
- **Certifying signature**: the first signature of a document can set what may change afterwards (no changes, form filling and signing, or those plus comments).
- **Lock the document after signing**: for the last signer; every field is locked and any later change shows up as a violation.

> **No certificate yet?**
>
> The **No certificate → create my own** link takes you to **Create certificate**. A certificate made there is self-signed: it proves the document's integrity, but legal validity needs a qualified e-signature.

## Verify signatures

When you open a signed PDF in the Viewer, a message appears at the top, such as "Signed and all signatures are valid." The **Signature panel** shows the details of each signature.

For a fuller check, open **Verify** from the **Security** list above the page title, choose the PDF and click **Verify**. For each signature you see:

- **Integrity**: whether the document changed after signing and, if so, whether the signature allows that change.
- **Trust**: whether the certificate chain ends at a root in your **Trusted roots**. Self-signed certificates show as not verified, with the reason.

To trust a provider's signatures, use **Add certificate or trust list** to add its root certificate (.cer, .crt, .pem or .der) or a trust list (an EU trusted list .xml or the Adobe AATL). **Check revocation online** is off by default; when on, it asks the issuer whether the certificate has been withdrawn.

## Create and export a certificate

On **Create certificate** in the **Security** list, enter your **Full name**, **E-mail**, **Organization** and **Country**, then choose the **Validity** and the **Key**. Under **Purpose**, choose **Signing documents**, **Receiving sealed documents** or **Both**. The certificate password needs at least 8 characters, and the result is saved as a .p12 file.

If someone wants to send you a document sealed so that only you can open it, use **Export public certificate**. It takes the public half of your .p12 and writes it as a .cer file; your private key never leaves the .p12. Sealing and password protection are covered on the [Security](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/security/) page.

vivePDF remembers the path of the .p12 you signed with, never its password. You can make it forget the path in **Settings › Data**; what is stored is explained on [Settings and privacy](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/settings-privacy/). Timestamps and the online revocation check are off while [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) is on.

---

# Security

> How to password-protect a PDF in vivePDF, set permissions, seal it with a certificate, add watermarks and stamps, strip hidden data and redact.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/security/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

vivePDF's security tools let you add a password and permissions to a PDF, remove a password, seal a file so that only chosen certificate holders can open it, add watermarks and stamps, clean out hidden data before sharing and permanently redact text. Every tool writes its result to a new file; your original stays as it was.

## Finding the tools

Open **Tools › Security**; the page starts on **Add password**. Click **Security** above the page title to list every tool in the group: **Add password**, **Remove password**, **Seal with a certificate**, **Open with a certificate**, **Redaction**, **Privacy check** and the [signing tools](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign/). **Add watermark**, **Stamp** and **Remove watermark** sit in the **Content editing** group. **Show all** in the **Tools** menu lists every tool as well.

## Passwords and permissions

1. On **Add password**, choose the PDF.
2. Type an **Open password**. It is needed to open the document; leave it empty if you only want to limit what people can do.
3. Type an **Owner password**. It is needed to change the permissions later.
4. Under **Permissions**, choose what is allowed, or use **Quick set**: **Everything allowed**, **Read only**, **No copying** or **Most restricted**.
5. Click **Add password**.

If you leave the owner password empty, a random one is created and shown once when the file is written. Keep it somewhere safe: it is the only way to lift the limits later. For **Encryption**, use **AES-256 (recommended)**; AES-128 and RC4 are only for older readers and cannot store letters such as ş, ğ or İ in a password. **Encrypt the file information too** also protects the title, author and subject.

New passwords are checked against a built-in list of common breached passwords. If you turn on the online check in **Settings › Web**, only the first 5 characters of the password's SHA-1 hash go to Have I Been Pwned, never the password itself.

**Remove password** creates a copy without a password; enter the open or the owner password. If the file is protected by permissions only, it works without one.

## Sealing with a certificate

**Seal with a certificate** encrypts the file so that only the holders of the private keys for the certificates under **Recipients** can open it, with no password at all. Add the recipients' public certificates with **Add a certificate**, then click **Seal**. Only RSA certificates can receive a sealed document.

To open a sealed file, use **Open with a certificate**: choose the **Sealed PDF**, the **Certificate (.p12 / .pfx)** that carries your private key and its password, then click **Open**. An unprotected copy is written. To give someone your own public certificate, see **Export public certificate** on [Sign and verify](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign/).

## Watermarks and stamps

In **Add watermark**, choose a **Watermark type**: **Text**, **Image** (PNG / JPG) or a **PDF page** from another file. A live preview shows the first page while you set the size, position and pages. **Show the watermark** can limit it to the screen or to print. **Burn the watermark into the page** turns marked pages into pictures, so the watermark can no longer be removed, but the text on those pages can no longer be selected or searched either.

**Stamp** puts a framed word at the chosen place on each page: pick a preset such as **APPROVED**, **DRAFT**, **CONFIDENTIAL** or **PAID**, or write your own. Placeholders such as `{date}`, `{name}`, `{page}` and `{total}` are filled in. Settings you use often can be kept under **Presets**.

**Remove watermark** scans the document and lists the watermarks it finds; tick the ones to remove. Check the result in the Viewer.

## Privacy check

**Privacy check** shows what a file reveals beyond its visible pages. Click **Scan document** to see findings such as metadata, XMP metadata, JavaScript and automatic actions, embedded files, comments, external links, hidden text, hidden layers, and camera and location details in photos. Tick the items under **What to remove** and click **Clean and save**.

> **Signed files**
>
> Cleaning a signed file writes a new file without a valid signature. If it has to stay signed, sign the cleaned copy again.

## Redaction

If sensitive text stays in the file, remove it for good with **Redaction**. Type words under **Text to find**, or pick kinds from **Sensitive data found**, such as IBANs, e-mail addresses or phone numbers, and add regular expressions if needed. Use **Count matches** to check first, then click **Redact**. Matching text is removed from the file and covered; this cannot be undone.

**Also remove matches outside the page** searches comments, form fields, bookmarks and document properties too. To black out an area by hand, open the document in the Viewer, choose **Edit › Page tools › Black out area**, drag over the area and click **Black out**. The full list of tools is on the [Tools](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/tools/) page.

---

# Write a document in Studio

> How to write reports, assignments and theses in the Studio document editor, with headings, tables, footnotes, references, columns and PDF export.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/studio-document/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

The Studio document editor lets you write a report, article, assignment or thesis inside vivePDF and turn it into a properly paginated PDF. While you type, the preview on the right shows the finished pages, and the cover, contents, page numbers, footnotes and reference list fall into place on their own.

## Start a new document

1. Click **Studio** in the top bar. You can also get there from the **Write a document** card in **Tools › Show all**, or from the command palette with `Ctrl+K`.
2. Under **Start a document**, pick a starting point: **Blank document**, **Report**, **Letter**, **Petition**, **Assignment**, **Meeting minutes**, **Lecture notes**, **Booklet**, **CV** or **Invoice**.
3. Start typing. To return to a document you left unfinished, choose **Continue** on the **Continue your document** card.

If you already have the text, **Import text…** turns a plain text, Markdown or web page file into a document.

## Formatting

The formatting bar above the editor keeps everything you use often in one place:

- **Paragraph style** switches between **Normal text** and **Heading 1** to **Heading 4**. The table of contents is built from these headings.
- **Bold**, **Italic**, **Underline**, **Strikethrough**, **Superscript**, **Subscript**, **Text colour** and **Highlight** format the text; **Format painter** copies formatting from one place to another, and **Clear formatting** removes it.
- **Bulleted list**, **Numbered list** and **Checklist** add lists; **Quote**, **Code block**, **Link**, **Insert picture**, **Insert symbol**, **Horizontal line** and **Page break** sit on the same bar.
- The **Line and paragraph spacing** menu sets line spacing, space before and after, and first-line indent for the selected paragraphs.

From the keyboard, `Ctrl+Alt+1`, `2` and `3` apply heading levels, `Ctrl+Shift+8` and `Ctrl+Shift+7` start lists, and `Shift+Enter` breaks the line without starting a new paragraph. The full list is on the [Keyboard shortcuts](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/) page.

### Tables

Place a table with **Insert table**. While the cursor is inside it, table buttons appear on the bar: **Add row below**, **Add column to the right**, **Delete row**, **Delete column**, **Merge cells**, **Split cell**, **Header row on or off** and **Delete table**.

## Footnotes

The **Insert footnote** button, or `Ctrl+Alt+F`, puts a numbered marker at the cursor and opens the note panel below. Write the note, then click **Back to the text**. Each footnote is printed at the foot of the page its marker lands on; if the notes grow too long for the page, they become endnotes under **Notes** at the end of the document. A note can hold citations and small pictures too.

## Sources and references

**Citations and references** on the formatting bar opens the **Sources** window:

- **Import file** loads a BibTeX, RIS or CSL JSON library; **Paste** adds entries copied from Zotero, Mendeley or EndNote; **New source** lets you type one in.
- **Add by DOI** fetches the details from doi.org and needs internet; only the DOI is sent. **Add from PDF** finds the DOI inside an article's PDF on your computer and then fetches its details the same way. With offline mode on, neither goes online.
- Choose a **Citation style**: **APA 7**, **MLA 9**, **Chicago (author-date)** or **IEEE**. **Insert citation** places a citation in the text and **Insert reference list** adds the list.
- **Check sources** asks Crossref whether any of your sources has been retracted or corrected.

To start from a source library, the **Bibliography** card in the tool catalogue opens a document with this window already open.

## Page settings and columns

The **Preview** tab in the side panel shows how the PDF will look. The **Settings** tab holds:

- **Page**: **Paper size** (A4, A5, B5, Letter, Legal), **Orientation**, **Margins**, **Columns** and **Column gap**.
- **Text**: **Font**, **Size**, **Line spacing**, **Heading colour**, and a separate heading font if you want one.
- **Header and footer**: header and footer text, plus **Page numbers**.
- **Table of contents**: **Add a table of contents** and how many heading levels it shows.
- **Cover**: **Add a cover page** in the **Classic**, **Colour band**, **Frame** or **Minimal** style.

To set part of the document in a different number of columns, use the **Section break** menu on the formatting bar. **Section break: 2 columns** starts the next page in two columns, while **Continuous section break: 2 columns** carries on on the same page, so a full-width title can sit above two-column text.

## Find and replace, word count

The search button at the top, or `Ctrl+F`, opens the **Find and replace** bar; `Ctrl+H` opens it with the replace field showing. **Match case** and **Whole words only** narrow the search, and **Replace all** changes every match in one step that a single undo reverses.

The word and character count is always shown below the editor. When you select text, it shows the words in the selection alongside the total.

## Save and export

`Ctrl+S` saves a vivePDF document (`.vivedoc`) that you can reopen and keep editing. For the finished file, click **Export** or press `Ctrl+E` and choose a **File type**:

- **PDF**: with its cover, contents, page numbers and bookmarks. The text stays selectable.
- **Markdown**: headings, lists, tables, links, pictures and footnotes are kept; colours, fonts and the page layout are left out.

For free-form work such as posters, invitations or business cards, see [Design in Studio](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/studio-design/). To change a PDF you already have, start from the [Tools](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/tools/) list.

---

# Design in Studio

> How to design posters, certificates and invitations from templates in Studio, build a CV, prepare print-ready business cards, use layers and export.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/studio-design/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

Studio is vivePDF's design editor for posters, certificates, invitations, social posts, business cards and similar work on a free canvas, saved as a PDF or as pictures. You can start from more than 170 templates and drag text, shapes, pictures and QR codes into place.

## Start a design

Click **Studio** in the top bar. The start page offers several ways in:

- **Start from a template**: templates are grouped into categories such as **Certificates**, **Invitations**, **Posters**, **Menus**, **Social media** and **Flyers and brochures**; **Search templates** finds one by name.
- **Start with a blank page**, or use **Custom size** to type the width and height yourself and click **Create**.
- **Business cards** opens a card with a front and a back (see below).
- **Build a CV** opens the form-based CV builder (see below).
- **Open design…** opens a design you saved, and **Recent designs** lists the ones you worked on last. Unfinished work waits on the **Continue where you left off** card.

## Add and edit items

The panel on the left has four tabs: **Elements**, **Templates**, **Layers** and **Data**.

1. On the **Elements** tab, add text with **Add a heading**, **Add a subheading** or **Add body text**. **Shapes**, **Icons**, **Tables and charts**, **Ornaments**, **Picture** and **QR code** are there too.
2. Click an item to select it. Change its colour, font, size, shadow or alignment in the properties panel.
3. Drag the item to move it, and use the handles to resize or rotate it. A right-click offers commands such as **Duplicate**, **Bring to front**, **Group**, **Lock** and **Copy style**.

You can also add items from the keyboard: `T` adds text, `R` a rectangle, `O` an ellipse, `L` a line and `A` an arrow. In the design editor, `F1` or `?` shows every shortcut; the list is also on the [Keyboard shortcuts](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/) page.

### Layers and pages

The **Layers** tab lists the items on this page. Drag a layer to change the order, or press `Alt+↑` or `Alt+↓` on it; you can hide and lock items from here as well. Double-click a group to pick one item inside it.

In the page strip, **Add page** adds a page and **All pages** shows every page so you can drag them into a new order. The **View** menu turns **Rulers**, **Guides**, **Margins**, **Bleed area (3 mm)** and **Snapping** on and off.

### Many copies from a table

On the **Data** tab, choose **Connect a table** and pick a CSV or Excel file. Clicking a column adds it as a placeholder to the selected text or QR code. When you export, every row of the table becomes its own copy of the design with its values filled in, which suits certificates or name badges.

## CV builder

**Open CV builder** shows a form on the **Content** tab: personal details, experience, education, skills, languages and more. The CV preview updates as you type.

- **Fill with sample** loads an example CV; **Import from PDF…** reads an existing CV or a LinkedIn PDF and brings its sections into the form.
- On the **Design** tab, pick a design such as **Classic**, **Modern** or **ATS-friendly**, and set the **Accent colour**, **Photo shape**, **Spacing**, **Paper** and **CV language**.
- **Export** saves the CV as PDF, PNG or JPG. For freer changes, choose **Edit freely in Studio**.

## Business cards

**Business cards** on the start page opens a card with **Front** and **Back** pages. Sizes include 85 × 55, 90 × 50, US 3.5 × 2 in, square and mini; **Rounded corners** in the page panel shows the corner the printer will cut.

Select an item and, under **Print finish**, apply **Embossed**, **Debossed**, **Letterpress**, **Foil** (gold, silver, copper, rose gold or holographic) or **Spot UV gloss**. The effect is simulated on screen. If you set a QR code's content to **Contact card**, scanning it lets a phone save your contact details.

> **Before you send it to the printer**
>
> In the export window, turn on **Print-ready PDF**. It adds **Bleed** (usually 3 mm) and **Trim marks**; **Finish plates** turns foil and gloss into separate spot colours or separate pages for the print shop. Choose A4 or SRA3 as the **Sheet** and the cards are laid out on one sheet, with the backs mirrored so they line up when printed double-sided.

## Save and export

`Ctrl+S` saves your work as a vivePDF design that you can open again later. For the finished file, click **Export** or press `Ctrl+E`:

- Choose PDF, PNG or JPG as the **File type**. Under **Pages**, take every page, the current page or a range such as `1-3, 5`.
- For pictures, set the **Resolution** and **JPG quality**; pages whose background is set to **None** are saved see-through with **See-through background**.
- With **Keep it editable in Studio** on, the design is stored inside the PDF, so opening that PDF in vivePDF lets you edit it in Studio again. **Sign the PDF** adds an invisible digital signature with your .p12 or .pfx certificate; there is more about signatures on the [Sign and verify](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/sign/) page.

`Ctrl+P` sends the design straight to the printer. For long text such as a report or thesis, [Write a document in Studio](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/studio-document/) is the better fit.

---

# Present a PDF

> How to present a PDF full screen in vivePDF, from F5 to the pen and laser, black and white boards, speaker notes and the two-screen presenter view.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/present/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

vivePDF turns any PDF into a full-screen slide show without a separate presentation program. While you present, you can draw on the page, use a laser pointer or spotlight, switch to a black or white board, and with a projector connected see your notes on your own screen only.

## Start a presentation

1. Open the PDF in the **Viewer**. The [Open and read a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-and-read/) page explains how.
2. Press `F5` to start from the first page, or `Shift+F5` to start from the page you are on. `F11` (`⌃``⌘``F` on a Mac) enters and leaves presentation mode too.
3. Move between pages with the arrow keys, `Page Up` and `Page Down`. `G` opens the **Slide overview** with every slide; click one to jump there.
4. Press `Esc` to finish. Each `Esc` takes exactly one step back: first it puts the tool away, then it leaves the board, and last it ends the presentation.

The presentation toolbar appears when you move the pointer to the bottom edge of the screen.

## Drawing and pointing tools

Pick a tool from the toolbar or with a single key:

| Key | Tool |
|---|---|
| `L` | Laser pointer |
| `P` | Pen |
| `H` | Highlighter |
| `E` | Eraser |
| `S` | Spotlight |
| `M` | Magnifier |
| `U` | On-screen ruler |
| `Z` | Zoom to a dragged area |
| `V` | Select, move or delete drawings |

The **Shapes** menu on the toolbar holds **Line**, **Arrow**, **Rectangle**, **Ellipse** and **Measure length**, and **Text** lets you type on the page.
