For a selected drawing, `R` and `Shift+R` rotate it right and left, `Ctrl+D` duplicates it and `Del` deletes it. `Ctrl+Z` and `Ctrl+Y` undo and redo drawing.

The on-screen ruler shows real centimetres; drag it to move or turn it, and lines drawn along its edge come out straight.

Defaults for the pen colour and width, the laser colour and the spotlight size are in **Settings › Presentation**. Every presentation shortcut is listed on the [Keyboard shortcuts](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/) page.

## Black and white boards

`B` or `.` turns the screen black and `W` turns it white. Use the empty screen to draw the audience's attention back to you, or draw on it like a whiteboard. A board has its own **Board tools** bar: select, pen, highlighter, shapes and eraser, colours that suit the board, size presets, undo and redo, **Clear board** and **Back to slides**. Each board keeps its own undo history.

## Notes, timer and clock

- `N` shows or hides the **Speaker notes** panel for the current page. Notes are kept page by page and shared with presenter view.
- `T` shows or hides the timer, and `C` the clock.
- If a page contains code, `K` opens the detected code blocks and moves between them.

## Presenter view (two screens)

With a projector or second screen connected, press `Alt+F5` or click **Presenter view** on the Viewer toolbar; `Alt+Shift+F5` starts from the page you are on. The projector shows only the slide. Your screen shows the **Current page**, a large **Next page** preview, the **Elapsed** time, the **Clock** and your **Speaker notes**.

- The preview's arrows let you look further ahead without changing the projector; clicking a preview jumps the presentation there.
- The pen, laser, spotlight and boards appear on the projector too.
- **Swap screens** trades the roles of the two screens, and **End presentation** closes it.
- Notes are saved in the app's data folder on this computer; the PDF itself is not changed.

> **If only one screen is visible**
>
> When the projector mirrors your screen, vivePDF shows **Only one screen is visible**. On Windows, press `Windows+P`, choose **Extend**, then click **Try again**. You can also carry on with **Present on this screen** or **Rehearse in a window**.

If the document has unsaved changes, the projector shows the file as it is saved on disk, so vivePDF first asks you to choose between **Save and present** and **Present anyway**.

## Insert items while presenting

The **Insert** (+) button on the presentation toolbar and in the presenter console offers **Add formula**, **Add shape**, **Add function graph**, **Add molecule**, **Add table**, **Add chart**, **Add flowchart**, **Add diagram (Mermaid)**, **Add question** and **Add answer key**. Prepare the item, then click the page to place it; `Esc` cancels. You can move and resize a placed item like a drawing and double-click it to edit it again. The Insert menu works on the black and white boards too.

## Keep or discard drawings

Presentation drawings and inserted items are temporary by default. When you leave the presentation, vivePDF asks **Keep the presentation drawings?**:

- **Save to the PDF** writes the drawings into the PDF as annotations; board drawings are added as new pages at the end.
- **Discard drawings** removes them all.
- **Decide later** keeps them as an unsaved change; they are written into the PDF when you save the document.

To keep permanent notes every time, set **Drawings** to **Permanent notes** in **Settings › Presentation**. For the rest of the settings, see [Settings and privacy](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/settings-privacy/).

---

# Settings and privacy

> Every vivePDF settings section, what Help › Privacy says goes online, and how to remove the data kept on this computer in Settings › Data.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/settings-privacy/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

All of vivePDF's preferences live in **Settings**: appearance, startup, where results are saved, reading, presentation, tools, updates and data. vivePDF collects no personal data; **Help › Privacy** lists when the app touches the network and what it keeps on this computer, and **Settings › Data** removes it.

## Opening Settings

Open Settings from the top bar. The list on the left gathers the sections into three groups: **Application**, **Viewing** and **System and data**. If you do not know where a setting lives, type its name into **Search settings…** at the top. Language and theme changes apply immediately.

## The sections

### Application

- **Appearance**: language, theme (Light, Dark, or System to follow the Windows theme), **Interface scale**, **Interface zoom** and **Reduce motion**.
- **Startup and privacy**: **Continue where I left off**, **Remember recent files**, **Keep operation history**, **Ask before closing**, **Keep a backup before saving**, **Keep running in the tray** and **Start with the system**.
- **Files**: whether tools write their result **Next to the source** or to a **Fixed folder**, the file **Name pattern**, and what happens **After an operation** (do nothing, show in Explorer or open the file).
- **Web**: the **Search engine** for the Viewer's right-click menu, the online check for new passwords, and **Offline mode**.

### Viewing

- **Viewer**: thumbnail size, default side panels, **Opening zoom**, two-page view, text selection colour, **Author name for comments** and **Reload when the file changes**.
- **Reading & read aloud**: reading mode defaults, speech rate, default voice, offline voice models and translation languages.
- **Presentation**: pen, laser pointer and spotlight defaults, and whether drawings are **Temporary** or kept as **Permanent notes**. See [Present a PDF](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/present/) for more.

### System and data

- **Tools**: OCR language packs, the LibreOffice-based **Office converter**, the default OCR language and the default compression.
- **Updates**: the installed version, **Check for updates** and **Check automatically at startup**. Installing always asks you first; see [Installation](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/).
- **System** (Windows): **Open PDF files with vivePDF**, Windows default apps, an Explorer **Context menu** and a “Send to” shortcut.
- **Data**: everything stored on this computer, described below.
- **Feedback**: **Report a bug**, **Suggest a feature**, the **Log folder** and **Diagnostics**, which copies version details to the clipboard.

## Help › Privacy

Open **Privacy** from the **Help** menu in the top bar. The page shows two lists:

- **Network access**: documents, passwords and certificates never leave this computer. Only things you start go online: update checks, voice models, language packs, fonts and LibreOffice when you click **Download** or **Install**, web search, turning a web page into a PDF, DOI lookups, the optional leaked-password check and a timestamp while signing. Bug reports are never sent automatically.
- **Stored on this computer**: recent files, the session snapshot, settings, the path of the certificate you signed with (never its password), backups, the search index, operation history, watch-folder rules, saved signatures, downloaded packs and the local log file.

The top of the page also shows whether [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) is on or off; **Open setting** takes you straight to the switch.

## Settings › Data

This section shows everything that is stored, with a count, and lets you remove each item:

- **Recent files** and **Operation history**: **Clear**.
- **Session snapshot**: **Delete**.
- **Remembered certificate path**: **Forget**.
- **Search index**: **Clear all**; indexed folders then have to be indexed again from the Search page.
- **Search history**, **Saved signatures**, **Watch-folder rules** and **Saved batch chains**: **Clear**.
- **Remembered chain passwords**: **Forget all** removes them from the system keychain.

> **Removed data does not come back**
>
> Most clear and delete actions ask you to confirm first. What you remove cannot be restored.

**Reset all settings** returns your preferences to their defaults only; recent files, history, saved signatures, chains and watch rules are kept. If you tick **Also delete saved signatures, chains, watch rules and presets** in the confirmation, those are deleted for good as well.

Downloaded language packs and voice models are removed in their own sections (**Tools**, **Reading & read aloud**); backups and the log file stay in their folders. More about the log file is on [Troubleshooting](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/troubleshooting/).

---

# Offline mode

> How to turn on Offline mode in vivePDF, what it stops, what keeps working without the internet and how features show that they are off.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

Offline mode stops every internet connection vivePDF makes with a single switch: update checks, downloads, web searches and lookups, opening web pages and online checks. Because the PDF tools already run on this computer, everything else keeps working without the internet. Your documents never leave this computer, whether the mode is on or off.

## Turn on Offline mode

1. Open **Settings** from the top bar.
2. Go to the **Web** section in the **Application** group.
3. Turn on **Offline mode**.

The mode is off by default. You can also see its state at the top of **Help › Privacy**: "Offline mode is on" or "Offline mode is off". **Open setting** there takes you straight to the switch.

## What it stops

While the mode is on, every feature that needs the internet is switched off:

- **Updates**: no automatic check at start-up, and **Settings › Updates** shows "Not checked: offline mode is on".
- **Downloads**: OCR language packs, read-aloud voices, translation languages, missing fonts in Studio and the LibreOffice download.
- **Web searches**: **Search on the web**, **Search picture with Google Lens** and **Google Translate** under **Translate** in the Viewer's right-click menu.
- **Web pages**: the **Web page → PDF** conversion.
- **Online checks**: the Have I Been Pwned check for new passwords, the timestamp server while signing, **Check revocation online** while verifying, and DOI lookups and checks in Studio.
- **GitHub**: **Open on GitHub** in a bug report and **Refresh from GitHub** in About.

This is not only a matter of the interface: the PDF engine also refuses requests that would go online while the mode is on.

## What keeps working

Everything that does not need the internet works as usual:

- Opening, reading, searching, organising pages, merging, splitting, compressing, converting, signing, password protection and every other PDF tool.
- [OCR](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/) with installed languages, read aloud with installed voices and the **Offline translator** with installed languages.
- Word, Excel and PowerPoint [conversions](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/convert/) through the LibreOffice that comes with the Windows installer.
- Studio, presentations and presenter view.
- **Help topics**, the keyboard shortcut list, **Save support bundle…** and copying a bug report or saving it to a file.

> **Download first, then switch off**
>
> If you will work on a computer without internet, download the OCR languages, voices and translation languages you need first, then turn on Offline mode. Downloaded packs stay on this computer and work offline.

## How switched-off features look

Offline mode does not hide anything. Buttons stay where they are but are greyed out and cannot be clicked; hovering over one shows "Off while offline mode is on (Settings › Web)".

Sections that download things (such as the OCR language packs in **Settings › Tools**) and the **Web page → PDF** screen show a note: "Offline mode is on, so nothing is downloaded or looked up on the internet." **Change** beside the note takes you to **Settings › Web**.

Offline mode only stops vivePDF's own connections; it does not cut your computer's internet connection, so your browser and other apps carry on as usual.

If an action still needs the internet, you see the message "This needs the internet, but offline mode is on." Switching the mode off brings everything back straight away; you do not need to restart the app.

For the full list of when vivePDF goes online and what it stores on this computer, see [Settings and privacy](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/settings-privacy/).

---

# Keyboard shortcuts

> vivePDF keyboard shortcuts, the per-screen list that F1 opens, saving it as a PDF, the macOS key equivalents and the full list for every screen.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/shortcuts/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

Most things you do often in vivePDF have a keyboard shortcut: opening a document, searching, zooming, presenting or formatting in Studio. This page groups the shortcuts by screen, and the same list is always one key away inside the app.

## The shortcut list in the app

On any screen, press `F1` or `Ctrl+/` to open the **Shortcuts** window, which shows only the shortcuts that work on that screen. In the **Viewer**, for example, you see the viewing, editing and presentation shortcuts; in the **Page organizer**, the page shortcuts; and in Studio, those of the document or design editor. The general shortcuts that work everywhere are added to each list. Press `F1` during a presentation and the list shows only the presentation shortcuts, so you can find a key without leaving the slides.

You can reach the same window in other ways too:

- **Help › Keyboard shortcuts (F1)** in the top bar.
- **Keyboard shortcuts for this screen** in the command palette, which opens with `Ctrl+K`.

The **Search shortcuts** box at the top narrows the list. The buttons at the bottom do the following:

- **Save as PDF** turns the list on screen into a PDF you can print and keep beside the keyboard.
- **All shortcuts** opens the complete list with every group, whichever screen you are on.
- **Help topics** goes to the help topic for the current screen. `Shift+F1` does the same.

In the Studio design editor, `F1` or `?` opens the editor's own shortcut window. See [Design in Studio](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/studio-design/) for more.

## Keys on macOS

On a Mac, vivePDF shows its shortcuts with Mac keys:

- `⌘` (Command) takes the place of `Ctrl`, `⌥` (Option) of `Alt`, and `⇧` of `Shift`.
- Full screen is `⌃``⌘``F` instead of `F11`.
- On Mac keyboards, function keys such as `F1` and `F5` may also need `fn`, depending on your keyboard settings.

The **Windows · Linux** and **macOS** buttons just below change which keys the lists show. The full list of shortcuts, grouped by screen, follows below.

# Tools

> Where to open vivePDF's 86 tools, what each of the thirteen tool categories is for, and a searchable list with a short description of every tool.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/tools/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

vivePDF has 86 tools, from merging and OCR to conversion and digital signatures, all sorted into thirteen categories. This page explains where to open them and what each category is for; the short description of every tool is in the list below.

## Open a tool

There are three ways to reach a tool:

- **Tools menu**: click **Tools** in the top bar. The categories are listed on the left with the number of tools in each; point at one and its tools appear on the right with a short description. **Show all** at the bottom of the menu opens the **Tools** catalogue, which lists every tool with a search box. **Search in folders** searches inside the PDFs in a folder.
- **Home**: the **Tools** section has a **Search tools** box and a button for each group; choose **All** or a group to narrow the list. To keep the ones you use most in **Quick access**, use **Customize home**.
- **Command palette**: press `Ctrl+K`, or click the **Search tools, pages or documents** box in the top bar, type the tool's name and press `Enter`.

The rest of the top bar and the palette are covered on the [Interface](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/interface/) page.

## The thirteen categories

- **Page layout**: tools that change the order, number and size of pages: merging, splitting, the page organiser, rotating, deleting and extracting pages, cropping, page size, booklets and posters. More on the [Organise pages](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/pages/) page.
- **Optimisation**: compressing, repairing, OCR, flattening and PDF/A archiving.
- **Check**: comparing two documents, accessibility, print check, the thesis check and the privacy check.
- **Scan**: scanning from a scanner or a photo, cleaning up scans and splitting a scanned batch into documents.
- **To PDF**: tools that make a PDF from pictures, Office documents, SVG drawings and web pages.
- **From PDF**: tools that turn a PDF into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, pictures, SVG, text, Markdown, HTML or EPUB, or pull out its pictures. See [Convert files](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/convert/).
- **Create & design**: writing a document and designing in Studio, Create PDF, CVs, business cards, books, documents from a table, paper and bibliographies.
- **Content editing**: tools that work on what is on the page: editing text, find and replace, page numbers, headers and footers, cover pages, letterheads, background colour, bookmarks, automatic links and document info.
- **Marks & codes**: adding and removing watermarks, stamps, adding QR codes and reading codes.
- **Forms & exams**: filling forms, mail merge, exporting form data as a table, detecting fields, and creating and grading answer sheets.
- **Read & review**: mark-up, comments, attachments, reading aloud, translating and printing.
- **Security & signing**: signing and verifying, adding and removing passwords, redaction, sealing and opening with a certificate, and creating and exporting certificates. See [Security](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/security/).
- **Automation**: batch runs, watched folders and renaming files.

Every tool follows below, by category and with a short description; type in the box above the list to find the one you need straight away.

## Page layout

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Merge | Combine several PDFs into one file, in order. |
| Split | Cut by ranges, page count, size or bookmarks. |
| Page organizer | Drag to reorder, rotate, delete and insert pages. |
| Rotate PDF | Permanently rotate selected pages. |
| Delete pages | Delete pages, or everything before/after one. |
| Extract pages | Create a new PDF from selected pages. |
| Crop | Trim margins with millimetre precision. |
| Page size | Shrink or enlarge pages to A6, A5, A4, A3, A2, Letter or a custom size. |
| Booklet / N-up | Lay out 2, 4 or 9 pages per sheet, or build a booklet. |
| Poster / tiles | Print one page large across several sheets, with cut marks. |

## Optimisation

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Compress | Resample images and shrink the file. |
| Repair | Repair a damaged PDF that will not open. |
| OCR | Turn scanned pages into searchable text. |
| Flatten | Bake forms and annotations into the content. |
| PDF/A archive | Check a PDF for long-term archiving and save a PDF/A-2b copy. |

## Check

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Compare | Find text and visual differences between two files. |
| Accessibility | Score a PDF against accessibility basics and fix title, language and alternative text. |
| Print check | Checks fonts, image resolution, bleed and colour spaces before printing. |
| Thesis check | Checks a finished thesis for margins, fonts, line spacing and page numbers. |
| Privacy check | See what a file reveals (metadata, scripts, attachments, links, ID numbers) and clean it before sharing. |

## Scan

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| From scanner | Scan straight from a connected scanner into a PDF. |
| From photo | Turn phone photos of paper into a straightened PDF. |
| Enhance | Straighten, clean and whiten scanned pages. |
| Split batch | Cut a batch scan into documents at blank pages, QR sheets or text. |

## To PDF

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Images → PDF | Turn JPG, PNG, WebP files or a whole folder into a PDF. |
| Office → PDF | Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML, Markdown → PDF (LibreOffice is downloaded on request). |
| SVG → PDF | Turn SVG drawings, logos and icons into a sharp, vector PDF. |
| Web page → PDF | Save a web page as a PDF, with or without its pictures. |

## From PDF

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| PDF → Word | Convert to a Word document, layout preserved. |
| PDF → Excel | Detect tables and export them to Excel. |
| PDF → PowerPoint | Export each page as a PowerPoint slide. |
| PDF → JPG / PNG | Export pages as JPG, PNG or WebP. |
| Extract images | Pull every embedded picture out of a PDF in its original quality. |
| PDF → SVG | Turn each page into a vector SVG drawing that opens in Inkscape, Illustrator or Figma. |
| PDF → Text | Export as a plain text file. |
| PDF → Markdown | Produce Markdown that keeps headings and tables. |
| PDF → HTML | Convert pages to an HTML document. |
| PDF → EPUB | Turn a PDF into a reflowable EPUB for phones and e-readers. |

## Create & design

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Write a document | Write a report, article or thesis with headings, tables, citations and a contents list. |
| Design in Studio | Posters, flyers, invitations and social posts on a free canvas with 170+ templates. |
| Create PDF | Turn plain text or Markdown into a report, letter, petition, minutes or booklet |
| CV builder | A CV with a classic, modern or compact template, photo and clickable contacts |
| Business card | Two-sided cards with foil, emboss and spot UV, print-ready with bleed and imposition. |
| Book | Markdown or text chapters as a book with a cover, linked contents and page numbers |
| Documents from a table | Certificates, invitations and name badges for every row of a CSV or Excel table |
| Paper | Blank, lined, graph, dot grid or music paper as a ready-to-print PDF |
| Bibliography | Import .bib, RIS or CSL JSON, edit sources and export an APA, MLA, Chicago or IEEE reference list. |

## Content editing

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Edit text | Change existing text in place (experimental). |
| Find and replace | Find text and rewrite it in the same size and colour. |
| Page numbers | Add page numbers wherever you like. |
| Header / footer | Write a header and footer on every page. |
| Cover page | Put a designed cover page in front of a PDF: title, author, institution, logo or photo |
| Letterhead | Lay a template PDF under or over every page. |
| Background colour | Puts a plain colour under the pages, or removes one added earlier. |
| Bookmarks | Edit the table of contents or generate it from headings. |
| Auto-link | Make web addresses and e-mail addresses in the text clickable. |
| Document info | Shows page count, page size, file size, PDF version and encryption, and edits title, author, subject and keywords. |

## Marks & codes

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Add watermark | Apply a text or image watermark. |
| Remove watermark | Remove text, annotation or repeated-image watermarks. |
| Stamp | Stamp a document as approved, draft or confidential. |
| Add QR code | Stamp a QR code with a link or running number onto pages. |
| Read codes | List every QR code and barcode found in a document. |

## Forms & exams

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Fill | Fill form fields, optionally lock them. |
| Mail merge | Fill one form from every row of a CSV or Excel table. |
| Export table | Collect the values of many filled forms into one spreadsheet. |
| Detect fields | Turn underlines and boxes into real form fields. |
| Create answer sheets | Print bubble answer sheets that can be read back from a scan. |
| Grade answer sheets | Read filled answer sheets, grade them against a key and export the scores. |

## Read & review

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Annotate / mark up | Add highlights, drawings, shapes and text boxes. |
| Comments | Read, reply to and resolve comments, and export or import them as XFDF or FDF. |
| Attachments | See, add, save and remove files attached to a PDF. |
| Read aloud | Reads the document aloud with voices that work without internet. |
| Translate | Translates selected text between installed languages without internet. |
| Print | Prints all, some, odd or even pages with scaling, copies and pages per sheet. |

## Security & signing

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Sign | Apply a PAdES signature with a PFX / P12 certificate. |
| Verify | Check signature integrity and coverage. |
| Add password | Protect with a password and permissions. |
| Remove password | Remove the password and save an open copy. |
| Redaction | Permanently remove text and areas. |
| Seal with a certificate | Seal a file for certificate holders, with no password at all. |
| Open with a certificate | Open a certificate-sealed file with your own certificate. |
| Create certificate | Generate a self-signed certificate. |
| Export public certificate | Write the public .cer out of a .p12 you already hold. |

## Automation

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Batch | Applies the same operation to several documents at once. |
| Watched folders | Run a saved chain automatically on every new PDF in a folder. |
| Rename | Name files after their content: date, invoice number, title or amount. |

---

# Release notes

> The main changes in each vivePDF version, how updates reach you and where to find the complete list of changes.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/release-notes/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

This page lists the main changes that came with each version of vivePDF. The notes below match the **What's new** section inside the app: the newest version comes first, each under its own heading. They cover the highlights only; for every small fix, see the complete list.

## How updates arrive

vivePDF checks for new versions itself and tells you when one is out. At start-up it only fetches version information; downloading and installing always ask you first.

1. Open **Settings › Updates** and click **Check for updates**. The same command is also in the **Help** menu.
2. When a new version is out, a **v… ready** label appears in the top bar. Choose **Download and install**; the update arrives signed.
3. Once the download finishes, click **Restart** and the app opens on the new version.

The **Installed version** line on the same screen shows which version you have. If you do not want automatic checks, turn off **Check automatically at startup**. While [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) is on, no check is made at all. Installing and uninstalling are covered on the [Installation](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/) page.

### After an update

The first time you start the new version, vivePDF shows its highlights once in a window titled **vivePDF … is installed**. After you close it, the same notes are always available under **Help › What's new**.

## The complete list of changes

Every addition, change and fix in each version is recorded with its date in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) on GitHub. The installers and a short note for each version are on the [releases page](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases).

## vivePDF 0.5.0

- A renewed reference manager: a DOI becomes a reference in the official APA 7, MLA, Chicago, IEEE, ISNAD, Vancouver and Harvard styles, and .bib files are read correctly, edited and saved back into their own file.
- Conversions to Word, PowerPoint, Excel and HTML are far closer to the PDF: fonts, links, pictures, tables and columns stay in place, and scanned tables reach Excel row by row.
- The print dialog shows a preview of each sheet next to the settings, with your chosen pages, pages per sheet, grayscale and scale.
- Make vivePDF the app that opens your PDF files from Settings › System, on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- New tools: PDF → SVG and Background colour; Comments, Attachments, Read aloud, Translate and Print now also sit in the tool categories.
- Wide Excel tables fit the paper, missing fonts are named before converting, Images → PDF can compress photos, and pictures can be extracted as the page shows them.
- The Studio document editor works like Word: a ribbon with tabs, rulers, page lines and page setup, a navigation pane, and thesis tools: numbered headings, figure and table captions with their lists, and roman page numbers before the main text.
- Thesis writing in the Studio: ready Master's and Doctoral thesis starters with common university rules, equations typed in LaTeX and numbered (1), (2)… for reference, comments with replies beside the page, and export to Word with the contents, footnotes, equations and comments.
- Thesis check and review: Tools › Thesis check checks a finished thesis PDF against university rules for paper, margins, font, line spacing, headings and page numbers; in a Studio document, Track changes marks inserted and deleted text with its author, lets you accept or reject one or all, and goes to Word as real tracked changes; version history keeps a version on every save and every 10 minutes, with a preview and restore.

## vivePDF 0.4.0

Released: 2026-10-21 · [GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases/tag/v0.4.0)

- Word, Excel and PowerPoint files open straight in vivePDF as PDFs, also from Open With in Finder and Explorer; when LibreOffice is missing, vivePDF offers to set it up and opens the file once it is ready.
- Tabs work like a browser's: drag a tab or a whole tab group out to open it in its own window where you drop it, or onto another vivePDF window to move it there.
- vivePDF runs on the Mac: full screen keeps the window buttons beside the logo, Command shortcuts and the menu bar work the macOS way, trackpad pinch zooms smoothly, and updates arrive inside the app.
- The black and white presentation boards have a toolbar with pen, highlighter, shapes and eraser, pick several drawings at once and undo up to 100 steps.
- Smoother and lighter: scrolling a PDF no longer stutters, typing stays quick in long Studio documents, and page previews no longer wait for each other.

## vivePDF 0.3.0

Released: 2026-10-15 · [GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases/tag/v0.3.0)

- Help that works offline: F1 shows the shortcuts of the screen you are on (and saves them as a PDF), Help › Help topics explains the main tasks step by step, and bug reports can carry pictures and sample files in a support package you save yourself.
- Offline mode: one switch in Settings › Web turns off every feature that would use the internet — updates, downloads, web search, citation lookups and the leaked-password check.
- Presenter view: the projector shows only the slides while your laptop shows the next page, a timer and speaker notes.
- Studio documents learned Word-style writing tools: footnotes, columns and section breaks, find and replace, line spacing, symbols, word count and Markdown export.
- Presentations can insert formulas, shapes, charts, tables and diagrams on the fly, also on the black and white boards.

## vivePDF 0.2.0

Released: 2026-10-09 · [GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases/tag/v0.2.0)

- Studio has 174 templates, with new CV layouts, ornaments and redesigned business documents, planners and labels.
- The CV builder imports an existing CV or LinkedIn PDF and gains undo, reordering and month pickers.
- The page organizer selects pages by shape, size or text, drags pages out to the desktop or onto another tab, and saves pages as pictures.
- The viewer fills in forms on the page, copies text blocks and pictures between documents, highlights selected text and edits bookmarks.
- Home collections can be rearranged, searched and recoloured, and recent files can be pinned.

## vivePDF 0.1.1

Released: 2026-10-04 · [GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases/tag/v0.1.1)

- Studio: a design editor for making a PDF from scratch, with ready-made templates for certificates, invitations, cards, posters and more.
- The CV builder fills a form on the left and shows the finished CV on the right.
- Studio pictures can be cropped and adjusted, and designs gain tables, charts, flowcharts, formulas, shadows and rulers.
- A library of 24 open-licence fonts, all with Turkish letters, downloads on request.
- More than 1,600 icons can be searched by name in your language and added as sharp, recolourable drawings.

# FAQ

> Short answers about vivePDF's price, privacy, offline use, supported systems, signing, OCR languages and updates.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/faq/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

Here are the questions people ask most often about vivePDF, with short answers. If yours is not here, have a look at [Troubleshooting](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/troubleshooting/).

## Is vivePDF free?

Yes, vivePDF is completely free. Every tool is included, and there are no paid tiers, accounts or usage limits.

## Are my files uploaded to a server?

No. Your documents, passwords and certificates never leave your computer; all the work happens on it. Help › Privacy lists every case in which the app goes online.

## Does it work without an internet connection?

Yes, the tools do not need an internet connection. Only things such as update checks, downloading language packs or turning a web page into a PDF go online. Offline mode in Settings › Web stops all of those connections with one switch.

## Which operating systems does it run on?

Ready-made installers are available for Windows 10 and Windows 11 (64-bit) and for Macs with Apple silicon on macOS 14 Sonoma or later. On Linux, vivePDF is built from source.

## Is vivePDF open source?

Yes. All of the source code is published on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 licence. You can read it, build it yourself and change it.

## Can I edit the existing text in a PDF?

Yes. In Edit › Edit text, click a run of text on the page to change its text, size or colour. The new text is written in the document's own font at the same size; if it does not fit, it is shrunk and you are told.

## Can I sign a PDF with a digital certificate?

Yes. Tools › Sign applies a PAdES signature with your .p12 or .pfx certificate and also verifies signed files. If you have no certificate, vivePDF can create a self-signed one; it proves the document has not changed, but legal validity needs a qualified e-signature.

## Which languages can OCR read?

Turkish and English come with the app. Packs for about 40 languages can be downloaded in Settings › Tools › OCR language packs; each is downloaded once and then works offline.

## How do I update vivePDF?

The app checks for new versions itself and asks before downloading anything. To check by hand, click Check for updates in Settings › Updates, then choose Download and install and Restart.

## Does it collect usage data or telemetry?

No. vivePDF collects no usage data, identifiers or crash reports, and it does not ask you to create an account. Bug reports are never sent automatically either.

## Where do I report a bug?

Help › Report a bug opens a report window where you can copy the report, save it to a file or open it as a prefilled GitHub issue in your browser. Nothing is sent automatically, and you can also go straight to the Issues section of the vivePDF repository on GitHub.

## Which languages is the interface available in?

The interface comes in eight languages: Turkish, English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese and Arabic. Arabic is shown right to left.

---

# Troubleshooting

> What to do when a vivePDF tool fails, with the log folder, support bundle, bug reports, SmartScreen, missing LibreOffice and OCR language packs.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/troubleshooting/
Last updated: 2026-10-18

When something in vivePDF does not work as expected, start by reading the message on screen: it says what went wrong and usually how to fix it. If the problem stays, the log folder, support bundle and bug report in the **Help** menu let you see what happened and pass it on to us.

## First steps

- If a tool fails, try again with a copy of the file. Tools leave the original alone and write their result to a new file.
- If you see "The file is not a valid PDF or is damaged.", try the **Repair** tool on it first. The [Tools](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/tools/) page lists every tool.
- If a feature is greyed out and hovering shows "Off while offline mode is on", [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) is on. Turn it off in **Settings › Web**.
- Press `Shift+F1` for the help topic of the screen you are on, or `F1` for that screen's shortcuts.

## The SmartScreen warning at install

The installer carries no code signature, so the first time you run it Windows may show **Windows protected your PC**. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. See [Installation](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/) for details.

## "Cannot be opened" on a Mac

If macOS blocks vivePDF the first time, open **System Settings › Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway** next to the vivePDF message. You only need this once; see [Installation](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/) for details.

## "LibreOffice is required for this conversion."

Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversions use LibreOffice. If you see this message, open the **Office converter** part of **Settings › Tools**:

- On Windows, LibreOffice comes with the installer. **Install from the app package** sets it up without the internet (about 900 MB on disk).
- Without the package, **Download and install** downloads LibreOffice (about 350 MB).
- If LibreOffice is already on your computer, the status reads **Found on this computer** and that copy is used.

If LibreOffice is "still in use", close any open LibreOffice windows and try again. A password-protected Office file needs its password removed first, in the application that created it.

## "OCR language data not found."

OCR needs a language pack for the language of the text. In **Settings › Tools**, find the language under **OCR language packs** and click **Download**; each language is downloaded once. **Default OCR language** in the same section sets the one chosen for you. Downloading needs Offline mode to be off. More on the [OCR](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/ocr/) page.

## If the app closes

If vivePDF closes unexpectedly, the next start shows "vivePDF closed unexpectedly last time — Report the crash"; **Report** opens a report straight away. **Restore session** on Home brings your open documents back. If you see "The PDF engine could not be started.", close the app and open it again; if that does not help, save a support bundle.

## The log folder

**Help › Open log folder** opens the folder with the log files. The log records what happened in technical terms and never the contents of your documents. Error lines may include file paths, with your home folder shown as `~`. You can also reach it from **Settings › Feedback › Log folder**.

## Support bundle

**Help › Save support bundle…** gathers the system details and recent logs into one zip file you can share.

1. Choose **Help › Save support bundle…**.
2. Pick where to save it; the file name starts with `vivepdf-support-` and includes the date.
3. Use **Show in folder** in the "Support bundle saved" notification to find the file, then attach it to an issue or an e-mail.

The bundle is never sent anywhere by itself; you decide who gets it.

## Report a bug

**Help › Report a bug** opens the **Send a report** window. Choose the type (**Crash**, **Bug** or **Idea**) and describe what happened. If you like, tick **Include diagnostic information**; **What will be included** then shows exactly what goes into the report.

- Paste a screenshot with `Ctrl+V`, or add a sample file with **Add file…**. Attachments only go into a package you save with **Save as package (.zip)**; copying and GitHub never include them.
- **Open on GitHub** opens a prefilled issue in your browser. **Copy to clipboard** and **Save report to file** are there if you want to send the report another way.

> **Reports are never sent automatically**
>
> vivePDF never sends a report by itself. To see open issues or file a new one, use the [GitHub issues page](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/issues).

---

# Web viewer for your site

> Show PDFs on your own website with one tag. The vivePDF web viewer runs in the visitor's browser, needs no server and is free under the MIT licence.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/web-viewer/
Last updated: 2026-10-31

The vivePDF web viewer shows a PDF inside your own web page: page thumbnails, the document's contents, search, links, text selection, print and download. Pages are drawn by PDFium in the visitor's browser, so nothing is uploaded anywhere and you need no server of your own. The viewer is a separate package under the MIT licence; the desktop app's code is not in it.

## Add it with a script tag

1. Load the viewer once per page:

   ```html
   <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@vivepdf/viewer@0/dist/vivepdf.js"></script>
   ```

2. Put a viewer where the PDF should appear and give it a height:

   ```html
   <vive-pdf src="/files/price-list.pdf" style="height: 80vh"></vive-pdf>
   ```

The script on your page is about 2 KB. The viewer itself and its PDF engine load only when the viewer scrolls into view, and the engine stays in the browser's cache after the first visit.

## Try it

Pick the settings below: the code for your page changes with them, and the preview shows the result with a sample PDF.

## Compared with Adobe PDF Embed API

| | vivePDF web viewer | Adobe PDF Embed API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account and key | None | An Adobe account and a client ID registered for your domain; on any other domain the preview is blocked |
| Price | Free | Free; Adobe's terms allow it to set usage limits |
| Licence | MIT, open source | Adobe's proprietary terms; the code may not be modified |
| Where the code is loaded from | Your own server, a CDN or npm | Adobe's server, as documented |
| Data sent to the maker | None; the visitor's browser talks only to your site and the CDN you chose | Usage information, including the address of the web page, the file size and the page count |
| Branding | None | A "Powered by Adobe Document Cloud" link is required; the viewer shows the Adobe Acrobat logo |
| Ways to show a document | Box, full window, inline, lightbox | Full window, sized container, in line, lightbox |
| Search | Yes | Yes |
| Comments and markup | No, reading only | Yes, in full window mode |
| Filling in forms | No, reading only | Yes, in full window mode |

The Adobe column comes from Adobe's [PDF Embed API documentation](https://developer.adobe.com/document-services/docs/overview/pdf-embed-api/gettingstarted/) and its [Developer Terms of Use](https://wwwimages2.adobe.com/content/dam/cc/en/legal/servicetou/Developer-Terms-en_US-20240618.pdf) (June 2024 edition), checked on 31 October 2026.

## Host the files yourself

Download `vivepdf-viewer-<version>.zip` from the [releases on GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/releases), copy its `dist` folder to your site and load `dist/vivepdf.js` from there. Keep the files of the folder together: the viewer looks for the rest next to the script.

## Use it from npm

```sh
npm install @vivepdf/viewer
```

```js
import "@vivepdf/viewer";
```

A bundler does not copy the viewer's own files. Copy `node_modules/@vivepdf/viewer/dist` to a public folder and tell the viewer where it is:

```html
<vive-pdf src="/files/price-list.pdf" assets="/vivepdf/"></vive-pdf>
```

## Settings

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `src` | Address of the PDF |
| `page` | Page to open on, from 1 |
| `zoom` | `fit-width`, `fit-page` or a percentage such as `150` |
| `mode` | `sized` (a box, the default), `full` (window height), `inline` (as tall as the document, scrolls with the page) or `lightbox` (opens over the page) |
| `theme` | `light`, `dark` or `auto` |
| `lang` | `tr` or `en`; without it the page's language is used |
| `accent` | Colour of buttons and highlights |
| `toolbar`, `search`, `print`, `download` | `false` hides that control |
| `filename` | Name used when the file is downloaded |

The viewer can also be driven from JavaScript: `open()` takes a file the visitor picked, `goTo()`, `setZoom()` and `search()` move around the document, and events report when it is ready, when the page changes and when a file cannot be opened. All of it is described in the [API reference](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/blob/main/apps/embed/docs/api.md).

## PDFs on another site

The PDF is fetched by the visitor's browser, so a file on another domain must allow your page to read it. That site has to send these headers with the PDF:

```text
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://your-site.example
Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Range
```

The second header lets the viewer download only the parts of a large file that are on screen. Without the first one, the viewer says the file could not be downloaded.

## Content Security Policy

If your site sends a Content Security Policy, the viewer needs a few entries in it: `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in `script-src` for its engine, `blob:` in `img-src` for the rendered pages and the PDF's site in `connect-src`; from a CDN also the CDN in `script-src`, `worker-src` and `connect-src`. It needs no `'unsafe-inline'` and no `'unsafe-eval'`. Tested policies for both setups, files on your own site and files from a CDN, are in the [CSP guide](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/blob/main/apps/embed/docs/csp.md).

---

# Build from source

> What you need to run vivePDF from its source code, how to start it in development mode, run the tests and build your own installer.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/build-from-source/
Last updated: 2026-10-24

You can build and run vivePDF from its source code. That is the way to use it on Linux and on Intel Macs, which have no ready-made package; it is also where you start if you want to contribute.

## Repository layout

All of the source code is in the [vivePDF repository on GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF). It has three main folders:

- `apps/desktop` — the desktop app: the Tauri 2 (Rust) shell and the interface, written in React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind v4. The PDF viewer is EmbedPDF.
- `sidecar` — the Python engine, built on PyMuPDF. The app starts it as a separate process; pdf2docx, OCRmyPDF, pyHanko and Tesseract are used here too.
- `scripts` — scripts that package the engine and prepare release builds.

## Prerequisites

- Node 22 and pnpm 10
- Rust (stable) and your platform's build tools; on macOS, the Xcode command line tools
- Python 3.12 or later and uv

## Run in development mode

1. Clone the repository:

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF.git
   cd vivePDF
   ```

2. Install the interface dependencies:

   ```sh
   cd apps/desktop
   pnpm install
   ```

3. Set up the Python engine's environment. In development mode the app runs the engine straight from source:

   ```sh
   cd ../../sidecar
   uv sync
   ```

4. Start the app:

   ```sh
   cd ../apps/desktop
   pnpm tauri dev
   ```

## Tests

Each layer has its own tests. Run the commands in the folder shown:

| Layer | Folder | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Interface unit tests | `apps/desktop` | `pnpm test` |
| Type check and lint | `apps/desktop` | `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` |
| RPC types between the interface and the engine | `apps/desktop` | `pnpm check:rpc` |
| Python engine | `sidecar` | `uv run pytest -x -q` |
| Rust shell | `apps/desktop/src-tauri` | `cargo test` |
| End to end, with the real app | `apps/desktop` | `pnpm e2e` |

The end-to-end tests drive the real app through its interface and run on Windows only; they also need `cargo install tauri-driver --locked`. Setup details and the tests with real-world and very large documents are described in [docs/TESTING.md](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md).

## Build an installer

For an installable package, first package the Python engine as a single folder. The script builds the engine, copies it to `apps/desktop/src-tauri/binaries/engine/` and stops if the copy fails its self-checks:

```sh
scripts/build-sidecar.sh
```

On Windows, `scripts/build-sidecar.ps1` does the same. Then build the app with the release configuration. Without the update signing key, turn the updater files off:

```sh
cd apps/desktop
pnpm tauri build --config src-tauri/tauri.release.conf.json --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
```

The packages are written under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`. On Linux these include a `.deb` and an AppImage; make the AppImage executable with `chmod +x` before starting it.

> **Office conversions**
>
> Builds you make yourself on macOS and Linux use the LibreOffice installed on the system for Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversions. The Windows installer that carries LibreOffice inside is built with `scripts/build-windows-release.ps1`.

How the official releases are built and published, including signing and the update channel, is in [docs/RELEASING.md](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md). For the licence that covers the code, see [License](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/license/).

---

# License

> What vivePDF's AGPL-3.0 licence means for users and for anyone distributing modified builds, plus the third-party components it uses.

URL: https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/license/
Last updated: 2026-10-19

vivePDF is free software released under version 3 of the GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL-3.0-only). You can use the app at no cost, read its source code, change it and share it; if you give a modified version to other people, you must also offer them its source code under the same licence.

> **Not legal advice**
>
> This page sums up the licence in plain words. The full text in the repository's [LICENSE](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/blob/main/LICENSE) file is what counts. If you are unsure about your situation, ask a lawyer.

## For users

There are no conditions on using vivePDF for personal work, at school or at work. No fee, account or licence key is needed, and there is no limit on how many computers you install it on.

- All of the source code is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF), so you can see for yourself what the app does.
- You can change the code as you like on your own computer and [build it from source](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/build-from-source/).
- The licence also states that the software comes without any warranty.

## For people distributing modified builds

The licence's conditions apply once you pass a copy of vivePDF, or a version you have changed, on to others:

- Offer the source code of the version you distribute, including your changes, to everyone who receives it.
- License the modified version under AGPL-3.0 as well; you cannot add further restrictions for the people who receive it.
- Keep the copyright and licence notices intact.
- If you let people use your modified version over a network, the AGPL asks you to offer them its source code too. That is the main difference from the GPL.

## Third-party components

vivePDF is built on open-source components that carry their own licences. Some of them:

- **MuPDF / PyMuPDF** (AGPL-3.0) — the PDF engine
- **Tesseract OCR** (Apache-2.0) — the OCR engine and its language models
- **LibreOffice** (MPL-2.0) — Office file conversions. The Windows installer carries The Document Foundation's signed LibreOffice installer unmodified.
- **pyHanko** (MIT) — digital signatures
- **pdf2docx** (GPL-3.0) — PDF to Word conversion
- **Tauri** (MIT / Apache-2.0) — the desktop shell

The full list, with each component's licence and role in the app, is in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](https://github.com/mtvrkan/vivePDF/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Inside the app, the **Licences** link on the **Help › About** page also lists the components and their licences.

## Code signing policy

Signing of the Windows releases is being set up through SignPath Foundation's programme for open-source projects: free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/). Until the first signed release, the installers carry no code signature (see [Installation](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/)).

- Every signed installer is built from the public source code on GitHub's own build servers (GitHub Actions); nothing is built or changed by hand before signing.
- Every release is approved by hand before it is signed.
- The updates the app installs itself are checked against a separate update signature in any case, so a changed file is never installed.

Team roles:

- Committers and reviewers: [Mehmet Türkan (mtvrkan)](https://github.com/mtvrkan)
- Approvers: [Mehmet Türkan (mtvrkan)](https://github.com/mtvrkan)

Privacy: vivePDF sends nothing about you or your documents to other networked systems. It goes online only for things you start or allow: update checks, downloads you choose (LibreOffice, fonts, language packs, voice models), web search, turning a web page into a PDF, DOI lookups, the optional leaked-password check and a timestamp while signing. [Offline mode](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/offline/) switches all of them off; [Settings and privacy](https://vivepdf.com/en/docs/settings-privacy/) has the details.
